core.title: Unsupervised one-to-many image translation
Iteratively unveiling new regions of interest in Deep Learning models
core.summary: A new framework is proposed that refines those saliency maps to generate segmentation masks over the ROI on the initial image, then applies those masks to apply over the original inputs, then evaluates the classifier on the masked inputs to identify previously overlooked ROI.

core.title: Learning to rank for censored survival data
core.summary: This work studies how three categories of loss functions, namely partial likelihood methods, rank methods, and the classification method based on a Wasserstein metric and the non-parametric Kaplan Meier estimate of the probability density to impute the labels of censored examples, can take advantage of right-censored examples.

core.title: Convergence Properties of Deep Neural Networks on Separable Data
core.summary: This work studies the case of binary classification and proves various properties of learning in such networks under strong assumptions such as linear separability of the data, and confirms empirical observations by proving that the classification error also follows a sigmoidal shape in nonlinear architectures.

core.title: Machine Learning for Combinatorial Optimization: a Methodological Tour d'Horizon
core.summary: A main point of the paper is seeing generic optimization problems as data points and inquiring what is the relevant distribution of problems to use for learning on a given task.

core.title: Extending the Framework of Equilibrium Propagation to General Dynamics
Quaternion Convolutional Neural Networks for End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition
core.summary: This paper proposes to integrate multiple feature views in quaternion-valued convolutional neural network (QCNN), to be used for sequence-to-sequence mapping with the CTC model, and reports that QCNNs obtain a lower phoneme error rate (PER) with less learning parameters than a competing model based on real-valued CNNs.

core.title: Predicting Tactical Solutions to Operational Planning Problems under Imperfect Information
core.summary: Results on the motivating application on load planning for rail transportation show that deep learning models produce accurate predictions in very short computing time, close to the lower bounds calculated based on sample average approximation of the stochastic prediction programs.

core.title: Dendritic cortical microcircuits approximate the backpropagation algorithm
core.summary: A novel view of learning on dendritic cortical circuits and on how the brain may solve the long-standing synaptic credit assignment problem is introduced, in which error-driven synaptic plasticity adapts the network towards a global desired output.

core.title: Learning of Sophisticated Curriculums by viewing them as Graphs over Tasks
BigBrain: 1D convolutional neural networks for automated sementation of cortical layers
Reinforced Imitation Learning from Observations
Learning Hierarchical Structures On-The-Fly with a Recurrent-Recursive Model for Sequences
core.summary: A hierarchical model for sequential data that learns a tree on-the-fly, i.e. while reading the sequence, that creates adaptive skip-connections that ease the learning of long-term dependencies is proposed.

core.title: Disentangling the independently controllable factors of variation by interacting with the world
core.summary: This work hypothesizes that some of the causal factors could be discovered if the learner is allowed to interact with its environment, and proposes a specific objective function to find such factors, and proves experimentally that it can indeed disentangle independently controllable aspects of the environment without any extrinsic reward signal.

core.title: On the Relation Between the Sharpest Directions of DNN Loss and the SGD Step Length
core.summary: Analysis of the dynamics of SGD in the subspace of the sharpest directions shows that they influence the regions that SGD steers to, the overall training speed, and the generalization ability of the final model.

core.title: Learning powerful policies and better dynamics models by encouraging consistency
Manifold Mixup: Learning Better Representations by Interpolating Hidden States
core.summary: Manifold Mixup achieves large improvements over strong baselines in supervised learning, robustness to single-step adversarial attacks, semi-supervised learning, and Negative Log-Likelihood on held out samples.

core.title: How can deep learning advance computational modeling of sensory information processing?
core.summary: It is discussed how DNNs are amenable to new model comparison techniques that allow for stronger conclusions to be made about the computational mechanisms underlying sensory information processing.

core.title: A Dataset of Topic-Oriented Human-to-Chatbot Dialogues
core.summary: The analysis of dataset statistics is provided and some possible improvements for future data collection experiments are outlined.

core.title: The Bottleneck Simulator: A Model-based Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
core.summary: The Bottleneck Simulator is proposed: a model-based reinforcement learning method which combines a learned, factorized transition model of the environment with rollout simulations to learn an effective policy from few examples.

core.title: Mutual Information Neural Estimation
core.summary: A Mutual Information Neural Estimator (MINE) is presented that is linearly scalable in dimensionality as well as in sample size, trainable through back-prop, and strongly consistent, and applied to improve adversarially trained generative models.

core.title: EnGAN: Latent Space MCMC and Maximum Entropy Generators for Energy-based Models
Image-to-image translation for cross-domain disentanglement
core.summary: This paper achieves better results for translation on challenging datasets as well as for cross-domain retrieval on realistic datasets and compares the model to the state-of-the-art in multi-modal image translation.

core.title: Dynamic Frame Skipping for Fast Speech Recognition in Recurrent Neural Network Based Acoustic Models
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

core.title: On the Spectral Bias of Neural Networks
core.summary: This work shows that deep ReLU networks are biased towards low frequency functions, and studies the robustness of the frequency components with respect to parameter perturbation, to develop the intuition that the parameters must be finely tuned to express high frequency functions.

core.title: MetaGAN: An Adversarial Approach to Few-Shot Learning
core.summary: This paper proposes a conceptually simple and general framework called MetaGAN for few-shot learning problems, and shows that with this MetaGAN framework, it can extend supervised few- shot learning models to naturally cope with unlabeled data.

core.title: The First Conversational Intelligence Challenge
core.summary: A task for formal human evaluation of chatbots that allows to test capabilities of chatbot in topic-oriented dialogue and demonstrates that current technology allows supporting dialogue on a given topic but with quality significantly lower than that of human.

core.title: Information Fusion in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation 1
core.venue: Signal Processing and Machine Learning for Biomedical Big Data

core.title: A Walk with SGD
core.summary: The dynamics of SGD when training over-parametrized DNNs are empirically studied to deduce that during most of the training, SGD explores regions in a valley by bouncing off valley walls at a height above the valley floor, corresponding to better generalization.

core.title: Learning Anonymized Representations with Adversarial Neural Networks
core.summary: A novel training objective for simultaneously training a predictor over target variables of interest (the regular labels) while preventing an intermediate representation to be predictive of the private labels is introduced.

core.title: »Deep Learning ist keine Religion«
Introduction to NIPS 2017 Competition Track
core.summary: The question arises: What, if anything, could NIPS add to this rich ecosystem of data science competitions?

core.title: Bayesian Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning
core.summary: The proposed method combines scalable gradient-based meta-learning with nonparametric variational inference in a principled probabilistic framework and is capable of learning complex uncertainty structure beyond a point estimate or a simple Gaussian approximation during fast adaptation.

core.title: Interpretable Convolutional Filters with SincNet
core.summary: This paper proposes SincNet, a novel Convolutional Neural Network that encourages the first layer to discover more meaningful filters by exploiting parametrized sinc functions, and shows that the proposed architecture converges faster, performs better, and is more interpretable than standard CNNs.

core.title: On the Iterative Refinement of Densely Connected Representation Levels for Semantic Segmentation
core.venue: 2018 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
core.summary: This paper systematically study the differences introduced by distinct receptive field enlargement methods and their impact on the performance of a novel architecture, called Fully Convolutional DenseResNet (FC-DRN), and reports state-of-the-art result on the Camvid dataset.

core.title: Depth with Nonlinearity Creates No Bad Local Minima in ResNets
core.summary: It is proved that depth with nonlinearity creates no bad local minima in a type of arbitrarily deep ResNets with arbitrary nonlinear activation functions, in the sense that the values of all local minata are no worse than the global minimum value of corresponding classical machine-learning models, and are guaranteed to further improve via residual representations.

core.title: Focused Hierarchical RNNs for Conditional Sequence Processing
core.summary: A mechanism for focusing RNN encoders for sequence modelling tasks which allows them to attend to key parts of the input as needed and generalize significantly better on synthetic tasks as compared to the baselines is presented.

core.title: Generalization of Equilibrium Propagation to Vector Field Dynamics
core.summary: This work presents a simple two-phase learning procedure for fixed point recurrent networks that generalizes Equilibrium Propagation to vector field dynamics, relaxing the requirement of an energy function.

core.title: h-detach: Modifying the LSTM Gradient Towards Better Optimization
core.summary: A simple stochastic algorithm is introduced that prevents gradients flowing through this path from getting suppressed, thus allowing the LSTM to capture such dependencies better and show significant improvements over vanilla L STM gradient based training in terms of convergence speed, robustness to seed and learning rate, and generalization.

core.title: Boundary Seeking GANs
core.summary: A method for training GANs with discrete data that uses the estimated difference measure from the discriminator to compute importance weights for generated samples, thus providing a policy gradient for training the generator and demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm with discrete image and character-based natural language generation.

core.title: On Training Recurrent Neural Networks for Lifelong Learning
core.summary: Evaluation on the proposed benchmark shows that the unified model is more suitable than the constituent models for lifelong learning setting, and both these models are proposed in the context of feedforward networks and the feasibility of using them for recurrent networks.

core.title: Deep Graph Infomax
core.summary: Deep Graph Infomax (DGI) is presented, a general approach for learning node representations within graph-structured data in an unsupervised manner that is readily applicable to both transductive and inductive learning setups.

core.title: Finding Flatter Minima with SGD
Combining Model-based and Model-free RL via Multi-step Control Variates
MaD TwinNet: Masker-Denoiser Architecture with Twin Networks for Monaural Sound Source Separation
core.venue: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
core.summary: This work builds upon the recently proposed Masker-Denoiser (MaD) architecture and enhances it with the Twin Networks, a technique to regularize a recurrent generative network using a backward running copy of the network.

core.title: An Empirical Study of Example Forgetting during Deep Neural Network Learning
core.summary: It is found that certain examples are forgotten with high frequency, and some not at all; a data set’s (un)forgettable examples generalize across neural architectures; and a significant fraction of examples can be omitted from the training data set while still maintaining state-of-the-art generalization performance.

core.title: Learning Speaker Representations with Mutual Information
core.summary: This work learns representations that capture speaker identities by maximizing the mutual information between the encoded representations of chunks of speech randomly sampled from the same sentence.

core.title: Deep convolutional networks for quality assessment of protein folds
core.summary: It is shown that deep convolutional networks can be used to predict the ranking of model structures solely on the basis of their raw three-dimensional atomic densities, without any feature tuning.

core.title: SGD Smooths The Sharpest Directions
Towards End-to-end Spoken Language Understanding
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: This study showed that the trained model can achieve reasonable good result and demonstrated that the model can capture the semantic attention directly from the audio features.

core.title: Learning deep representations by mutual information estimation and maximization
core.summary: It is shown that structure matters: incorporating knowledge about locality in the input into the objective can significantly improve a representation’s suitability for downstream tasks and is an important step towards flexible formulations of representation learning objectives for specific end-goals.

core.title: Learning General Purpose Distributed Sentence Representations via Large Scale Multi-task Learning
core.summary: This work presents a simple, effective multi-task learning framework for sentence representations that combines the inductive biases of diverse training objectives in a single model and demonstrates that sharing a single recurrent sentence encoder across weakly related tasks leads to consistent improvements over previous methods.

core.title: BabyAI: First Steps Towards Grounded Language Learning With a Human In the Loop
core.summary: The BabyAI research platform is introduced to support investigations towards including humans in the loop for grounded language learning and puts forward strong evidence that current deep learning methods are not yet sufficiently sample efficient when it comes to learning a language with compositional properties.

core.title: SGD S MOOTHS THE S HARPEST D IRECTIONS
core.summary: Noise in SGD controls the spectral norm and conditioning of the Hessian throughout the training, and the cause is due to the dynamics of neurons saturating their non-linearity along the largest curvature directions, thus leading to improved conditioning.

core.title: Speech and Speaker Recognition from Raw Waveform with SincNet
core.summary: This paper proposes SincNet, a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that encourages the first layer to discover meaningful filters by exploiting parametrized sinc functions, and shows that the proposed architecture converges faster, performs better, and is more computationally efficient than standard CNNs.

core.title: Towards Understanding Generalization via Analytical Learning Theory
core.summary: A novel measure-theoretic theory for machine learning that does not require statistical assumptions is introduced and a new regularization method in deep learning is derived and shown to outperform previous methods in CIFar-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN.

core.title: Modeling the Long Term Future in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
Probabilistic Planning with Sequential Monte Carlo methods
Modularity Matters: Learning Invariant Relational Reasoning Tasks
core.summary: Experimental results support the hypothesis that modularity is a robust prior for learning invariant relational reasoning, and show that very shallow ResMixNet models are capable of learning each of the two tasks well, attaining less than 2% and 1% test error on the MNIST Parity and the colorized Pentomino tasks respectively.

core.title: Manifold Mixup: Encouraging Meaningful On-Manifold Interpolation as a Regularizer
core.summary: This work proposes Manifold Mixup which encourages the network to produce more reasonable and less confident predictions at points with combinations of attributes not seen in the training set by training on convex combinations of the hidden state representations of data samples.

core.title: On the Spectral Bias of Deep Neural Networks
core.summary: It is shown that deep networks with finite weights (or trained for finite number of steps) are inherently biased towards representing smooth functions over the input space, and all samples classified by a network to belong to a certain class are connected by a path such that the prediction of the network along that path does not change.

core.title: A3T: Adversarially Augmented Adversarial Training
core.summary: A procedure to improve adversarial robustness of deep neural networks through enforcing representation invariance is investigated, to train the classifier jointly with a discriminator attached to one of its hidden layer and trained to filter the adversarial noise.

core.title: A Data-Efficient Framework for Training and Sim-to-Real Transfer of Navigation Policies
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
core.summary: This work introduces a robust framework that plans in simulation and transfers well to the real environment, consisting of the encoder and planner modules, and shows successful planning performances in different navigation tasks.

core.title: Combined Reinforcement Learning via Abstract Representations
core.summary: It is shown that the modularity brought by this approach leads to good generalization while being computationally efficient, with planning happening in a smaller latent state space, which opens up new strategies for interpretable AI, exploration and transfer learning.

core.title: The effects of negative adaptation in Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning
core.summary: It is shown that the adaptation in an algorithm like MAML can significantly decrease the performance of an agent in a meta-reinforcement learning setting, even on a range of meta-training tasks.

core.title: The Pytorch-kaldi Speech Recognition Toolkit
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: Experiments, that are conducted on several datasets and tasks, show that PyTorch-Kaldi can effectively be used to develop modern state-of-the-art speech recognizers.

core.title: Quantized Guided Pruning for Efficient Hardware Implementations of Convolutional Neural Networks
core.summary: This paper proposes a combination of a new pruning technique and a quantization scheme that effectively reduce the complexity and memory usage of convolutional layers of CNNs, and replace the complex Convolutional operation by a low-cost multiplexer.

core.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Chatbot (Short Version)
core.summary: MILA's MILABOT chatbot is capable of conversing with humans on popular small talk topics through both speech and text and consists of an ensemble of natural language generation and retrieval models, including neural network and template-based models.

core.title: Convolutional neural networks for mesh-based parcellation of the cerebral cortex
core.summary: It is shown experimentally on the Human Connectome Project dataset that the proposed graph convolutional models outperform current state-ofthe-art and baselines, highlighting the potential and applicability of these methods to tackle neuroimaging challenges, paving the road towards a better characterization of brain diseases.

core.title: Universal Successor Representations for Transfer Reinforcement Learning
core.summary: This work proposes to use universal successor representations (USR) to represent the transferable knowledge and a USR approximator (USRA) that can be trained by interacting with the environment that can effectively applied to new tasks.

core.title: Predicting Solution Summaries to Integer Linear Programs under Imperfect Information with Machine Learning
core.summary: This work proposes a methodology to quickly predict solution summaries to discrete stochastic optimization problems to solve intermodal containers on double-stack trains through supervised learning and a large number of deterministic problems that have been solved independently and offline.

core.title: Feature-wise transformations
Twin Regularization for online speech recognition
core.summary: This paper adds a regularization term that forces forward hidden states of a unidirectional recurrent network to be as close as possible to cotemporal backward ones, computed by a "twin" neural network running backwards in time.

core.title: DEFactor: Differentiable Edge Factorization-based Probabilistic Graph Generation
core.summary: This work proposes a model for conditional graph generation that is computationally efficient and enables direct optimisation of the graph and demonstrates favourable performance of the model on prototype-based molecular graph conditional generation tasks.

core.title: Low-memory convolutional neural networks through incremental depth-first processing
core.summary: An incremental processing scheme for convolutional neural network (CNN) inference, targeted at embedded applications with limited memory budgets, where individual input pixels are propagated through all parts of the network they can influence under the given structural constraints.

core.title: Sparse Attentive Backtracking: Temporal CreditAssignment Through Reminding
core.summary: A novel algorithm which only back-propagates through a few of these temporal skip connections, realized by a learned attention mechanism that associates current states with relevant past states is studied.

core.title: Representation Mixing for TTS Synthesis
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: A simple method for combining multiple types of linguistic information in a single encoder, named representation mixing, enabling flexible choice between character, phoneme, or mixed representations during inference.

core.title: Dynamic Neural Turing Machine with Continuous and Discrete Addressing Schemes
core.summary: The model outperforms long short-term memory and NTM variants, and provides further experimental results on the sequential MNIST, Stanford Natural Language Inference, associative recall, and copy tasks.

core.title: The representational geometry of word meanings acquired by neural machine translation models
core.summary: This work applies a recently-proposed heuristic method for training NMT models with very large vocabularies, and shows that this vocabulary expansion method results in minimal degradation of embedding quality, which indicates that NMT embeddings should be used in applications that require word concepts to be organised according to similarity and/or lexical function.

core.title: Boundary-Seeking Generative Adversarial Networks
core.summary: This work introduces a method for training GANs with discrete data that uses the estimated difference measure from the discriminator to compute importance weights for generated samples, thus providing a policy gradient for training the generator.

core.title: On integrating a language model into neural machine translation
core.summary: This work combines scores from neural language model trained only on target monolingual data with neural machine translation model and fusing hidden-states of these two models, and obtains up to 2 BLEU improvement over hierarchical and phrase-based baseline on low-resource language pair, Turkish English.

core.title: End-to-End Online Writer Identification With Recurrent Neural Network
STDP-Compatible Approximation of Backpropagation in an Energy-Based Model
core.summary: Simulations and a theoretical argument suggest that this rate-based update rule is consistent with those associated with spike-timing-dependent plasticity, and could be an element of a theory for explaining how brains perform credit assignment in deep hierarchies as efficiently as backpropagation does.

core.title: Residual Connections Encourage Iterative Inference
core.summary: It is shown that residual connections naturally encourage features of residual blocks to move along the negative gradient of loss as the authors go from one block to the next, and empirical analysis suggests that Resnets are able to perform both representation learning and iterative refinement.

core.title: The Consciousness Prior
core.summary: A new prior is proposed for learning representations of high-level concepts of the kind the authors manipulate with language, inspired by cognitive neuroscience theories of consciousness, that makes it natural to map conscious states to natural language utterances or to express classical AI knowledge in a form similar to facts and rules.

core.title: Count-ception: Counting by Fully Convolutional Redundant Counting
core.venue: 2017 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
core.summary: A novel deep neural network architecture adapted from the Inception family of networks called the Count-ception network is proposed, which results in a 20% relative improvement over the state of the art method by Xie, Noble, and Zisserman in 2016.

core.title: Dynamic Layer Normalization for Adaptive Neural Acoustic Modeling in Speech Recognition
core.summary: The experimental results show that the proposed Dynamic Layer Normalization (DLN) improves neural acoustic models in terms of transcription accuracy by dynamically adapting to various speakers and environments.

core.title: A robust adaptive stochastic gradient method for deep learning
core.venue: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
core.summary: An adaptive learning rate algorithm, which utilizes stochastic curvature information of the loss function for automatically tuning the learning rates and a new variance reduction technique to speed up the convergence.

core.title: A Structured Self-attentive Sentence Embedding
core.summary: A new model for extracting an interpretable sentence embedding by introducing self-attention is proposed, which uses a 2-D matrix to represent the embedding, with each row of the matrix attending on a different part of the sentence.

core.title: Generalization in Deep Learning
core.summary: This paper explains why deep learning can generalize well, despite large capacity and possible algorithmic instability, nonrobustness, and sharp minima, and proposes a family of new regularization methods, both data-dependent and data-independent generalization guarantees with improved convergence rates.

core.title: Plan, Attend, Generate: Planning for Sequence-to-Sequence Models
core.summary: A model which can plan ahead in the future when it computes its alignments between input and output sequences is developed, constructing a matrix of proposed future alignments and a commitment vector that governs whether to follow or recompute the plan.

core.title: Image Segmentation by Iterative Inference from Conditional Score Estimation
core.summary: This work extends previous work on score estimation by denoising autoencoders to the case of a conditional distribution, with a novel use of a corrupted feedforward predictor replacing Gaussian corruption and experimentally finds that the proposed iterative inference from conditional Score estimation by conditional denoised autoen coders performs better than comparable models based on CRFs or those not using any explicit modeling of the conditional joint distribution of outputs.

core.title: Z-Forcing: Training Stochastic Recurrent Networks
core.summary: This work unify successful ideas from recently proposed architectures into a stochastic recurrent model that achieves state-of-the-art results on standard speech benchmarks such as TIMIT and Blizzard and competitive performance on sequential MNIST.

core.title: The Octopus Approach to the Alexa Competition : A Deep Ensemble-based Socialbot
core.summary: This work presents a novel, large-scale ensemble-based system for the Amazon Alexa Prize competition that leverages state-of-the-art methods from deep learning and reinforcement learning and demonstrates that it yields substantial improvements over several baseline systems.

core.title: ACtuAL: Actor-Critic Under Adversarial Learning
core.summary: The GAN framework is reframed so that the generator is no longer trained using gradients through the discriminator, but is instead trained using a learned critic in the actor-critic framework with a Temporal Difference (TD) objective.

core.title: Sparse Attentive Backtracking : Towards Efficient Credit Assignment In Recurrent Networks
core.summary: Sarse Attentive Backtracking learns an attention mechanism over the hidden states in the past and selectively backpropagates through paths with high attention weights, which allows the model to learn long term dependencies while only backtracking for a small number of steps into the past.

core.title: Graph Attention Networks
Towards an Automatic Turing Test: Learning to Evaluate Dialogue Responses
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: An evaluation model that learns to predict human-like scores to input responses, using a new dataset of human response scores is presented and it is shown that the ADEM model’s predictions correlate significantly, and at a level much higher than word-overlap metrics such as BLEU, with human judgements at both the utterance and system-level.

core.title: Measuring the tendency of CNNs to Learn Surface Statistical Regularities
Use machine learning to find energy materials
core.summary: Artificial intelligence can speed up research into new photovoltaic, battery and carbon-capture materials, argue Edward Sargent, Alán Aspuru-Guzikand colleagues.

core.title: Fraternal Dropout
core.summary: A simple technique called fraternal dropout is proposed that takes advantage of dropout to train two identical copies of an RNN (that share parameters) with different dropout masks while minimizing the difference between their (pre-softmax) predictions.

core.title: Generalization in Deep Learning
core.summary: Non-vacuous and numerically-tight generalization guarantees for deep learning are provided, as well as theoretical insights into why and how deep learning can generalize well, despite its large capacity, complexity, possible algorithmic instability, nonrobustness, and sharp minima.

core.title: Multiscale sequence modeling with a learned dictionary
core.summary: This multi-scale model makes predictions over multiple, potentially overlapping multi-symbol tokens, which has the flexibility of character- level models while maintaining many of the performance benefits of word-level models.

core.title: Learning normalized inputs for iterative estimation in medical image segmentation
core.summary: This paper proposes and examines a design that takes particular advantage of recent advances in the understanding of both Convolutional Neural Networks as well as ResNets, and shows that a low‐capacity FCN model can serve as a pre‐processor to normalize medical input data.

core.title: Memory Augmented Neural Networks with Wormhole Connections
core.summary: It is suggested that memory augmented neural networks can reduce the effects of vanishing gradients by creating shortcut (or wormhole) connections to propagate the gradients more effectively and it helps to learn the temporal dependencies.

core.title: Maximum-Likelihood Augmented Discrete Generative Adversarial Networks
core.summary: This work derives a novel and low-variance GAN objective using the discriminator's output that follows corresponds to the log-likelihood, which is proved to be consistent in theory and beneficial in practice.

core.title: The representational geometry of word meanings acquired by neural machine translation models
core.summary: This work applies a recently-proposed heuristic method for training NMT models with very large vocabularies, and shows that this vocabulary expansion method results in minimal degradation of embedding quality, which indicates that NMT embeddings should be used in applications that require word concepts to be organised according to similarity and/or lexical function.

core.title: Sharp Minima Can Generalize For Deep Nets
core.summary: It is argued that most notions of flatness are problematic for deep models and can not be directly applied to explain generalization, and when focusing on deep networks with rectifier units, the particular geometry of parameter space induced by the inherent symmetries that these architectures exhibit is exploited.

core.title: A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks
core.summary: The analysis suggests that the notions of effective capacity which are dataset independent are unlikely to explain the generalization performance of deep networks when trained with gradient based methods because training data itself plays an important role in determining the degree of memorization.

core.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Chatbot
core.summary: MILA's MILABOT is capable of conversing with humans on popular small talk topics through both speech and text and consists of an ensemble of natural language generation and retrieval models, including template-based models, bag-of-words models, sequence-to-sequence neural network and latent variable neural network models.

core.title: Twin Networks: Matching the Future for Sequence Generation
core.summary: This work proposes a simple technique for encouraging generative RNNs to plan ahead, and hypothesizes that this approach eases modeling of long-term dependencies by implicitly forcing the forward states to hold information about the longer-term future (as contained in the backward states).

core.title: Independently Controllable Factors
core.summary: This work hypothesizes that some of the causal factors of variation could be discovered if the learner is allowed to interact with its environment and proposes a specific objective function to find such factors and proves experimentally that it can indeed disentangle independently controllable aspects of the environment without any extrinsic reward signal.

core.title: Equivalence of Equilibrium Propagation and Recurrent Backpropagation
core.summary: This work shows that it is not required to have a side network for the computation of error derivatives and supports the hypothesis that in biological neural networks, temporal derivatives of neural activities may code for error signals.

core.title: Gated Orthogonal Recurrent Units: On Learning to Forget
core.summary: A novel recurrent neural network (RNN)–based model that combines the remembering ability of unitary evolution RNNs with the ability of gated Rnns to effectively forget redundant or irrelevant information in its memory is presented.

core.title: Char2Wav: End-to-End Speech Synthesis
core.summary: Char2Wav is an end-to-end model for speech synthesis that learns to produce audio directly from text.

core.title: Learning to Compute Word Embeddings On the Fly
core.summary: This work provides a method for predicting embeddings of rare words on the fly from small amounts of auxiliary data with a network trained end-to-end for the downstream task and shows that this improves results against baselines whereembeddings are trained on the end task for reading comprehension, recognizing textual entailment and language modeling.

core.title: Learning Independent Features with Adversarial Nets for Non-linear ICA
core.summary: This work proposes to learn independent features with adversarial objectives which optimize such measures implicitly without the need to compute any probability densities, and shows that this strategy can easily be applied to different types of model architectures and solve both linear and non-linear ICA problems.

core.title: Variational Walkback: Learning a Transition Operator as a Stochastic Recurrent Net
core.summary: This work develops a method for directly learning arbitrarily parameterized transition operators capable of expressing non-equilibrium stationary distributions that violate detailed balance, thereby enabling us to learn more biologically plausible asymmetric neural networks and more general non-energy based dynamical systems.

core.title: Sparse Attentive Backtracking: Long-Range Credit Assignment in Recurrent Networks
core.summary: This work proposes an alternative algorithm, Sparse Attentive Backtracking, which might also be related to principles used by brains to learn long-term dependencies, and learns an attention mechanism over the hidden states of the past and selectively backpropagates through paths with high attention weights.

core.title: Les données au service du savoir
Independently Controllable Features
core.summary: This work proposes a naive method to find factors that explain or measure the effect of the actions of a learner, and test it in illustrative experiments.

core.title: Deep Complex Networks
core.summary: This work relies on complex convolutions and present algorithms for complex batch-normalization, complex weight initialization strategies for complex-valued neural nets and uses them in experiments with end-to-end training schemes and demonstrates that such complex- valued models are competitive with their real-valued counterparts.

core.title: Variance Regularizing Adversarial Learning
core.summary: This work proposes an additional method to train GANs by explicitly modeling the discriminator's output as a bi-modal Gaussian distribution over the real/fake indicator variables and observes that this new method, when trained together with a strong discriminator, provides meaningful, non-vanishing gradients.

core.title: Towards more hardware-friendly deep learning
Twin Networks: Using the Future as a Regularizer
core.summary: This paper introduces a simple way of encouraging the RNNs to plan for the future by introducing an additional neural network which is trained to generate the sequence in reverse order, and requires closeness between the states of the forward RNN and backward RNN that predict the same token.

core.title: Plan, Attend, Generate: Character-Level Neural Machine Translation with Planning
core.summary: A model that can plan ahead when it computes alignments between the source and target sequences not only for a single time-step but for the next k time-steps as well by constructing a matrix of proposed future alignments and a commitment vector that governs whether to follow or recompute the plan.

core.title: Variational Bi-LSTMs
core.summary: This work proposes a variant of the Bi-LSTM architecture that creates a dependence between the two paths (during training, but which may be omitted during inference) and acts as a regularizer and encourages the two networks to inform each other in making their respective predictions using distinct information.

core.title: FigureQA: An Annotated Figure Dataset for Visual Reasoning
core.summary: FigureQA is envisioned as a first step towards developing models that can intuitively recognize patterns from visual representations of data, and preliminary results indicate that the task poses a significant machine learning challenge.

core.title: Dendritic error backpropagation in deep cortical microcircuits
core.summary: A multi-area neuronal network model in which synaptic plasticity continuously adapts the network towards a global desired output is introduced, which approximates the classical error backpropagation algorithm and suggests a biological implementation of deep learning.

core.title: Improving Speech Recognition by Revising Gated Recurrent Units
core.summary: This work proposes to remove the reset gate in the GRU design, resulting in a more efficient single-gate architecture and replaces tanh with ReLU activations in the state update equations, and shows that the revised architecture consistently improves recognition performance across different tasks, input features, and noisy conditions when compared to a standard GRU.

core.title: Monaural Singing Voice Separation with Skip-Filtering Connections and Recurrent Inference of Time-Frequency Mask
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: A recurrent inference algorithm, a sparse transformation step to improve the mask generation process, and a learned denoising filter are introduced that learns and optimizes a source-dependent mask and does not need a post processing step.

core.title: ObamaNet: Photo-realistic lip-sync from text
core.summary: The first architecture that generates both audio and synchronized photo-realistic lip-sync videos from any new text is presented, and it is claimed that this architecture is the first to be composed of fully trainable neural modules.

core.title: GibbsNet: Iterative Adversarial Inference for Deep Graphical Models
core.summary: GibbsNet does away with the need for an explicit p(z) and has the ability to do attribute prediction, class-conditional generation, and joint image-attribute modeling in a single model which is not trained for any of these specific tasks.

core.title: A network of deep neural networks for Distant Speech Recognition
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: Despite the remarkable progress recently made in distant speech recognition, state-of-the-art technology still suffers from a lack of robustness, especially when adverse acoustic conditions characterized by non-stationary noises and reverberation are met.

core.title: Deep Learning for Patient-Specific Kidney Graft Survival Analysis
core.summary: A deep learning method is proposed that directly models the survival function instead of estimating the hazard function to predict survival times for graft patients based on the principle of multi-task learning, which outperforms other common methods for survival analysis.

core.title: Three Factors Influencing Minima in SGD
core.summary: Through this analysis, it is found that three factors – learning rate, batch size and the variance of the loss gradients – control the trade-off between the depth and width of the minima found by SGD, with wider minima favoured by a higher ratio of learning rate to batch size.

core.title: Multi-way, multilingual neural machine translation
core.summary: The first attention-based neural-MT for multi-way, multilingual translation is proposed and it outperforms strong conventional statistical machine translation systems on Turkish-English and Uzbek-English by incorporating the resources of other language pairs.

core.title: Mode Regularized Generative Adversarial Networks
core.summary: This work introduces several ways of regularizing the objective, which can dramatically stabilize the training of GAN models and shows that these regularizers can help the fair distribution of probability mass across the modes of the data generating distribution, during the early phases of training and thus providing a unified solution to the missing modes problem.

core.title: An Actor-Critic Algorithm for Sequence Prediction
core.summary: An approach to training neural networks to generate sequences using actor-critic methods from reinforcement learning (RL) that condition the critic network on the ground-truth output, and shows that this method leads to improved performance on both a synthetic task, and for German-English machine translation.

core.title: A Neural Knowledge Language Model
core.summary: A Neural Knowledge Language Model (NKLM) which combines symbolic knowledge provided by a knowledge graph with the RNN language model, and shows that the NKLM significantly improves the perplexity while generating a much smaller number of unknown words.

core.title: BinaryNet: Training Deep Neural Networks with Weights and Activations Constrained to +1 or -1
core.summary: BinaryNet, a method which trains DNNs with binary weights and activations when computing parameters’ gradient is introduced, which drastically reduces memory usage and replaces most multiplications by 1-bit exclusive-not-or (XNOR) operations, which might have a big impact on both general-purpose and dedicated Deep Learning hardware.

core.title: On Multiplicative Integration with Recurrent Neural Networks
core.summary: This work introduces a general and simple structural design called Multiplicative Integration, which changes the way in which information from difference sources flows and is integrated in the computational building block of an RNN, while introducing almost no extra parameters.

core.title: Invariant Representations for Noisy Speech Recognition
core.summary: This work focuses on investigating neural architectures which produce representations invariant to noise conditions for ASR, and evaluates the proposed architecture on the Aurora-4 task, a popular benchmark for noise robust ASR.

core.title: HeMIS: Hetero-Modal Image Segmentation
core.venue: International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
core.summary: A deep learning image segmentation framework that is extremely robust to missing imaging modalities, which learns, for each modality, an embedding of the input image into a single latent vector space for which arithmetic operations are well defined.

core.title: Collaborative filtering techniques for drug discovery par 7 M / t ( 3 ’ / 7
core.summary: This work has cast the problem from a statistical learning point of view, traced analogies with standard collaborative filtering techniques, and set up the general hypotheses that have to be tested in order to validate the multi-task learning approach, and showed that it is possible to learn a shared representation of the tasks.

core.title: The Variational Walkback Algorithm
The One Hundred Layers Tiramisu: Fully Convolutional DenseNets for Semantic Segmentation
core.venue: 2017 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
core.summary: The proposed DenseNets approach achieves state-of-the-art results on urban scene benchmark datasets such as CamVid and Gatech, without any further post-processing module nor pretraining, and has much less parameters than currently published best entries for these datasets.

core.title: Equilibrium Propagation: Bridging the Gap between Energy-Based Models and Backpropagation
core.summary: It is shown that multi-layer recurrently connected networks with 1, 2, and 3 hidden layers can be trained by Equilibrium Propagation on the permutation-invariant MNIST task, and it makes it more plausible that a mechanism similar to Backpropagation could be implemented by brains.

core.title: Binarized Neural Networks
core.summary: Near state-of-the-art results with BDNNs are obtained on the permutation-invariant MNIST, CIFAR-10 and SVHN datasets.

core.title: UOUS AND DISCRETE ADDRESSING SCHEMES
core.summary: The D-NTM is evaluated on a set of Facebook bAbI tasks and shown to outperform NTM and LSTM baselines and provide further experimental results on sequential MNIST, associative recall and copy tasks.

core.title: Professor Forcing: A New Algorithm for Training Recurrent Networks
core.summary: The Professor Forcing algorithm, which uses adversarial domain adaptation to encourage the dynamics of the recurrent network to be the same when training the network and when sampling from the network over multiple time steps, is introduced.

core.title: Feedforward Initialization for Fast Inference of Deep Generative Networks is biologically plausible
core.summary: This work finds conditions under which a simple feedforward computation is a very good initialization for inference, after the input units are clamped to observed values.

core.title: Learning Latent Multiscale Structure Using Recurrent Neural Networks
core.summary: A hierarchical recurrent neural network architecture is introduced that enables the model to adpatively capture the underlying temporal dependencies in sequences with different timescales while not using explicit boundary information.

core.title: NYU-MILA Neural Machine Translation Systems for WMT’16
core.summary: The proposed neural machine translation system is an attention-based encoder‐decoder with a subword-level encoder and a character-level decoder that provides benefits especially when translating a source language into other morphologically rich languages.

core.title: On Random Weights for Texture Generation in One Layer Neural Networks
core.summary: It is theoretically show that one layer convolutional architectures (without a non-linearity) paired with the an energy function used in previous literature, can in fact preserve and modulate frequency coefficients in a manner so that random weights and pretrained weights will generate the same type of images.

core.title: Former NASA chief unveils $ 100 million neural chip maker KnuEdge
core.summary: The Data-Driven Discovery team at the Moore Foundation has also been discussing open access, particularly as it relates to the publications generated by the authors' #MooreData researchers.

core.title: Batch-normalized joint training for DNN-based distant speech recognition
core.summary: Improving distant speech recognition is a crucial step towards flexible human-machine interfaces and one potential limitation of state-of-the-art technology lies in composing modules that are not well matched because they are not trained jointly.

core.title: Noisy Activation Functions
core.summary: This work proposes to exploit the injection of appropriate noise so that the gradients may flow easily, even if the noiseless application of the activation function would yield zero gradient, and establishes connections to simulated annealing, making it easier to optimize hard objective functions.

core.title: Drawing and Recognizing Chinese Characters with Recurrent Neural Network
core.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
core.summary: Under the RNN framework, a conditional generative model with character embedding is proposed for automatically drawing recognizable Chinese characters and can be recognized by the discriminative RNN model with high accuracy.

core.title: A promising approach to model such hierarchical and temporal representation is the multiscale
core.summary: A novel multiscale approach that can capture the latent hierarchical structure in the sequence by encoding the temporal dependencies with different timescales using a novel update mechanism is proposed and evaluated on character-level language modelling and handwriting sequence generation.

core.title: Understanding intermediate layers using linear classifier probes
core.summary: This work proposes to monitor the features at every layer of a model and measure how suitable they are for classification, using linear classifiers, which are referred to as "probes", trained entirely independently of the model itself.

core.title: A Hierarchical Latent Variable Encoder-Decoder Model for Generating Dialogues
core.summary: A neural network-based generative architecture, with stochastic latent variables that span a variable number of time steps, that improves upon recently proposed models and that the latent variables facilitate both the generation of meaningful, long and diverse responses and maintaining dialogue state is proposed.

core.title: Hierarchical Multiscale Recurrent Neural Networks
core.summary: A novel multiscale approach, called the hierarchical multiscales recurrent neural networks, which can capture the latent hierarchical structure in the sequence by encoding the temporal dependencies with different timescales using a novel update mechanism is proposed.

core.title: Theano: A Python framework for fast computation of mathematical expressions
core.summary: The performance of Theano is compared against Torch7 and TensorFlow on several machine learning models and recently-introduced functionalities and improvements are discussed.

core.title: Binarized Neural Networks
core.summary: A binary matrix multiplication GPU kernel is written with which it is possible to run the MNIST BNN 7 times faster than with an unoptimized GPU kernel, without suffering any loss in classification accuracy.

core.title: Machines Who Learn.
core.summary: The article discusses artificial intelligence and the machine learning known as deep learning, referencing the history of AI from the 1950s through the mid 2010s and the algorithms used in deep learning.

core.title: Towards a Biologically Plausible Backprop
core.summary: This work contributes several new elements to the quest for a biologically plausible implementation of backprop in brains by introducing a very general and abstract framework for machine learning, in which the quantities of interest are defined implicitly through an energy function.

core.title: Recurrent Neural Networks With Limited Numerical Precision
core.summary: This paper addresses the question of how to best reduce weight precision during training in the case of RNNs by presenting results from the use of different stochastic and deterministic reduced precision training methods applied to three major RNN types which are then tested on several datasets.

core.title: Context-dependent word representation for neural machine translation
core.summary: This paper proposes to contextualize the word embedding vectors using a nonlinear bag-of-words representation of the source sentence and proposes to represent special tokens with typed symbols to facilitate translating those words that are not well-suited to be translated via continuous vectors.

core.title: Dynamic Neural Turing Machine with Soft and Hard Addressing Schemes
core.summary: The D-NTM is evaluated on a set of Facebook bAbI tasks and shown to outperform NTM and LSTM baselines and provide further experimental results on sequential pMNIST, Stanford Natural Language Inference, associative recall and copy tasks.

core.title: Deep Directed Generative Models with Energy-Based Probability Estimation
core.summary: This work proposes to train a deep directed generative model (not a Markov chain) so that its sampling distribution approximately matches the energy function that is being trained, Inspired by generative adversarial networks.

core.title: Aprendizaje profundo. Tras años de decepciones, la inteligencia artiñcial está empezando a cumplir lo que prometia en sus comienzos gracias a esta potente técnica
Multi-Way, Multilingual Neural Machine Translation with a Shared Attention Mechanism
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: The proposed multi-way, multilingual neural machine translation approach enables a single neural translation model to translate between multiple languages, with a number of parameters that grows only linearly with the number of languages.

core.title: Zoneout: Regularizing RNNs by Randomly Preserving Hidden Activations
core.summary: This work proposes zoneout, a novel method for regularizing RNNs that uses random noise to train a pseudo-ensemble, improving generalization and performs an empirical investigation of various RNN regularizers, and finds that zoneout gives significant performance improvements across tasks.

core.title: Diet Networks: Thin Parameters for Fat Genomic
core.summary: A novel neural network parametrization is proposed which considerably reduces the number of parameters and the error rate of the classifier on tasks in which the input is a description of the genetic variation specific to a patient, the single nucleotide polymorphisms, yielding millions of ternary inputs.

core.title: Task Loss Estimation for Structured Prediction
Pointing the Unknown Words
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A novel way to deal with the rare and unseen words for the neural network models using attention is proposed using attention, which uses two softmax layers in order to predict the next word in conditional language models.

core.title: A Character-level Decoder without Explicit Segmentation for Neural Machine Translation
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This paper evaluates an attention-based encoder-decoder with a subword-level encoder and a character-level decoder on four language pairs using the parallel corpora from WMT'15 to ask a fundamental question: can neural machine translation generate a character sequence without any explicit segmentation?

core.title: Multiresolution Recurrent Neural Networks: An Application to Dialogue Response Generation
core.summary: A new class of models called multiresolution recurrent neural networks, which explicitly model natural language generation at multiple levels of abstraction, are introduced, which outperform competing models by a substantial margin and generate more fluent, relevant and goal-oriented responses.

core.title: Mollifying Networks
core.summary: This paper attacks the problem of optimization of highly non-convex neural networks objectives by starting with a smoothed -- or mollified -- objective function which becomes more complex as the training proceeds and shows improvements on various difficult optimization tasks.

core.title: On random weights for texture generation in one layer CNNS
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: It is theoretically show that one layer convolutional architectures (without a non-linearity) paired with the an energy function used in previous literature, can in fact preserve and modulate frequency coefficients in a manner so that random weights and pretrained weights will generate the same type of images.

core.title: Hierarchical Memory Networks
core.summary: A form of hierarchical memory network is explored, which can be considered as a hybrid between hard and soft attention memory networks, and is organized in a hierarchical structure such that reading from it is done with less computation than soft attention over a flat memory, while also being easier to train than hard attention overA flat memory.

core.title: Generalizable Features From Unsupervised Learning
core.summary: It is demonstrated that an unsupervised model, trained to predict future frames of a video sequence of stable and unstable block configurations, can yield features that support extrapolating stability prediction to blocks configurations outside the training set distribution.

core.title: Online and offline handwritten Chinese character recognition: A comprehensive study and new benchmark
core.summary: Although directMap+convNet can achieve the best results and surpass human-level performance, it is shown that writer adaptation in this case is still effective and a new adaptation layer is proposed to reduce the mismatch between training and test data on a particular source layer.

core.title: Big Data: Theoretical Aspects [Scanning the Issue]
core.summary: This special issue highlights a number of algorithmic approaches that are fundamental to data analysis, both in formulating and solving problems that relate to Big Data.

core.title: Quantized Neural Networks: Training Neural Networks with Low Precision Weights and Activations
core.summary: A binary matrix multiplication GPU kernel is programmed with which it is possible to run the MNIST QNN 7 times faster than with an unoptimized GPU kernel, without suffering any loss in classification accuracy.

core.title: Generating Factoid Questions With Recurrent Neural Networks: The 30M Factoid Question-Answer Corpus
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: The 30M Factoid Question-Answer Corpus is presented, an enormous question answer pair corpus produced by applying a novel neural network architecture on the knowledge base Freebase to transduce facts into natural language questions.

core.title: An Actor-Critic Algorithm for Structured Prediction
Towards End-to-End Speech Recognition with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
core.summary: This paper proposes an end-to-end speech framework for sequence labeling, by combining hierarchical CNNs with CTC directly without recurrent connections, and argues that CNNs have the capability to model temporal correlations with appropriate context information.

core.title: SampleRNN: An Unconditional End-to-End Neural Audio Generation Model
core.summary: It is shown that the model, which profits from combining memory-less modules, namely autoregressive multilayer perceptrons, and stateful recurrent neural networks in a hierarchical structure is able to capture underlying sources of variations in the temporal sequences over very long time spans, on three datasets of different nature.

core.title: Iterative Alternating Neural Attention for Machine Reading
core.summary: A novel neural attention architecture to tackle machine comprehension tasks, such as answering Cloze-style queries with respect to a document that outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in standard machine comprehension benchmarks such as CNN news articles and the Children's Book Test dataset.

core.title: Architectural Complexity Measures of Recurrent Neural Networks
core.summary: This paper proposes three architecture complexity measures of RNNs and rigorously proves each measure's existence and computability, and demonstrates that increasing recurrent skip coefficient offers performance boosts on long term dependency problems.

core.title: EmoNets: Multimodal deep learning approaches for emotion recognition in video
core.summary: This paper explores multiple methods for the combination of cues from these modalities into one common classifier, which achieves a considerably greater accuracy than predictions from the strongest single-modality classifier.

core.title: A Recurrent Latent Variable Model for Sequential Data
core.summary: It is argued that through the use of high-level latent random variables, the variational RNN (VRNN)1 can model the kind of variability observed in highly structured sequential data such as natural speech.

core.title: Oracle Performance for Visual Captioning
core.summary: This work investigates the possibility of empirically establishing performance upper bounds on various visual captioning datasets without extra data labelling effort or human evaluation, and demonstrates the construction of such bounds on MS-COCO, YouTube2Text and LSMDC.

core.title: Building End-To-End Dialogue Systems Using Generative Hierarchical Neural Network Models
core.summary: The recently proposed hierarchical recurrent encoder-decoder neural network is extended to the dialogue domain, and it is demonstrated that this model is competitive with state-of-the-art neural language models and back-off n-gram models.

core.title: Towards Biologically Plausible Deep Learning
core.summary: The theory about the probabilistic interpretation of auto-encoders is extended to justify improved sampling schemes based on the generative interpretation of denoising auto- Encoder, and these ideas are validated on generative learning tasks.

core.title: Equilibrated adaptive learning rates for non-convex optimization
core.summary: A novel adaptive learning rate scheme, called ESGD, based on the equilibration preconditioner is introduced, and experiments show that ESGD performs as well or better than RMSProp in terms of convergence speed, always clearly improving over plain stochastic gradient descent.

core.title: Deconstructing the Ladder Network Architecture
core.summary: An extensive experimental investigation of variants of the Ladder Network in which individual components are replaced or removed individual components to learn about their relative importance concludes that the most important contribution is made by the lateral connections, followed by the application of noise, and the choice of what is referred to as the 'combinator function'.

core.title: Montreal Neural Machine Translation Systems for WMT’15
core.summary: The Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms (MILA) submission to WMT’15 is to evaluate this new approach to NMT on a greater variety of language pairs, using the RNNsearch architecture, which adds an attention mechanism to the encoderdecoder.

core.title: Task Loss Estimation for Sequence Prediction
core.summary: This work proposes another method for deriving differentiable surrogate losses that provably meet the requirement of consistency with the task loss, and focuses on the broad class of models that define a score for every input-output pair.

core.title: Deep Learning
core.summary: Deep learning is making major advances in solving problems that have resisted the best attempts of the artificial intelligence community for many years, and will have many more successes in the near future because it requires very little engineering by hand and can easily take advantage of increases in the amount of available computation and data.

core.title: Denoising Criterion for Variational Auto-Encoding Framework
core.summary: It is shown that injecting noise both in input and in the stochastic hidden layer can be advantageous and a modified variational lower bound is proposed as an improved objective function in this setup and it is found that the proposed denoising variational autoencoder (DVAE) yields better average log-likelihood than the VAE and the importance weighted autoencoders on the MNIST and Frey Face datasets.

core.title: Using Recurrent Neural Networks for Slot Filling in Spoken Language Understanding
core.venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio Speech and Language Processing

core.title: Empirical performance upper bounds for image and video captioning
core.summary: This work investigates the possibility of empirically establishing performance upper bounds on various visual captioning datasets without extra data labelling effort or human evaluation, and demonstrates the construction of such bounds on MS-COCO, YouTube2Text and LSMDC.

core.title: Brain tumor segmentation with Deep Neural Networks
core.summary: A fast and accurate fully automatic method for brain tumor segmentation which is competitive both in terms of accuracy and speed compared to the state of the art, and introduces a novel cascaded architecture that allows the system to more accurately model local label dependencies.

core.title: Show, Attend and Tell: Neural Image Caption Generation with Visual Attention
core.summary: An attention based model that automatically learns to describe the content of images is introduced that can be trained in a deterministic manner using standard backpropagation techniques and stochastically by maximizing a variational lower bound.

core.title: Training opposing directed models using geometric mean matching
core.summary: This work proposes a new method, referred to as geometric mean matching (GMM), that is based on the idea that the generative model should be close to the class of distributions that can be modeled by the approximate inference distribution, and can be fitted to the training data to be the geometric mean of these two.

core.title: Blocks and Fuel: Frameworks for deep learning
core.summary: This work introduces two Python frameworks to train neural networks on large datasets: Blocks and Fuel, which provides a standard format for machine learning datasets.

core.title: On Using Monolingual Corpora in Neural Machine Translation
core.summary: This work investigates how to leverage abundant monolingual corpora for neural machine translation to improve results for En-Fr and En-De translation and extends to high resource languages such as Cs-En and De-En.

core.title: Describing Multimedia Content Using Attention-Based Encoder-Decoder Networks
core.summary: This paper describes systems that learn to attend to different places in the input, for each element of the output, for a variety of tasks: machine translation, image caption generation, video clip description, and speech recognition.

core.title: Neural Networks with Few Multiplications
core.summary: Experimental results show that this approach to training that eliminates the need for floating point multiplications can result in even better performance than standard stochastic gradient descent training, paving the way to fast, hardware-friendly training of neural networks.

core.title: STDP as presynaptic activity times rate of change of postsynaptic activity
core.summary: A weight update formula is introduced that is expressed only in terms of firing rates and their derivatives and that results in changes consistent with those associated with spike-timing dependent plasticity (STDP) rules and biological observations, even though the explicit timing of spikes is not needed.

core.title: ReSeg: A Recurrent Neural Network for Object Segmentation
core.summary: The proposed network, called ReSeg, is a structured prediction architecture for images centered around deep recurrent neural networks based on the recently introduced ReNet model for object classification that can challenge the state of the art in object segmentation and may have further applications in structured prediction at large.

core.title: Hierarchical Neural Network Generative Models for Movie Dialogues
core.summary: The recently proposed hierarchical recurrent encoder decoder neural network is extended and demonstrated that it is competitive with state-of-the-art neural language models and backoff n-gram models and can be improved considerably by bootstrapping the learning from a larger questionanswer pair corpus and from pretrained word embeddings.

core.title: ReNet: A Recurrent Neural Network Based Alternative to Convolutional Networks
core.summary: The proposed network, called ReNet, replaces the ubiquitous convolution+pooling layer of the deep convolutional neural network with four recurrent neural networks that sweep horizontally and vertically in both directions across the image.

core.title: End-to-end attention-based large vocabulary speech recognition
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: This work investigates an alternative method for sequence modelling based on an attention mechanism that allows a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to learn alignments between sequences of input frames and output labels.

core.title: Target Propagation
GSNs : Generative Stochastic Networks
core.summary: A novel training principle for generative probabilistic models that is an alternative to maximum likelihood and an interesting justication for dependency networks and generalized pseudolikelihood and dene an appropriate joint distribution and sampling mechanism, even when the conditionals are not consistent.

core.title: SCANNING THE ISSUE Big Data : Theoretical Aspects
core.summary: This special issue highlights a number of algorithmic approaches that are fundamental to data analysis, both in formulating and solving problems, and describes new approaches that incorporate data-driven learning methods in the development of advanced hash functions.

core.title: An objective function for STDP
core.summary: Spike-based simulations agree with the proposed relationship between spike timing and the temporal change of postsynaptic activity and show a strong correlation between the biologically observed STDP behavior and the behavior obtained from simulations where the weight change follows the gradient of the predictive objective function.

core.title: BinaryConnect: Training Deep Neural Networks with binary weights during propagations
core.summary: BinaryConnect is introduced, a method which consists in training a DNN with binary weights during the forward and backward propagations, while retaining precision of the stored weights in which gradients are accumulated, and near state-of-the-art results with BinaryConnect are obtained on the permutation-invariant MNIST, CIFAR-10 and SVHN.

core.title: Artificial Neural Networks Applied to Taxi Destination Prediction
core.summary: This work describes its first-place solution to the ECML/PKDD discovery challenge on taxi destination prediction by using an almost fully automated approach based on neural networks and ranking first out of 381 teams.

core.title: A Hierarchical Recurrent Encoder-Decoder for Generative Context-Aware Query Suggestion
core.venue: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
core.summary: This work presents a novel hierarchical recurrent encoder-decoder architecture that makes possible to account for sequences of previous queries of arbitrary lengths and is sensitive to the order of queries in the context while avoiding data sparsity.

core.title: Attention-Based Models for Speech Recognition
core.summary: The attention-mechanism is extended with features needed for speech recognition and a novel and generic method of adding location-awareness to the attention mechanism is proposed to alleviate the issue of high phoneme error rate.

core.title: Variance Reduction in SGD by Distributed Importance Sampling
core.summary: This work proposes a framework for distributing deep learning in which one set of workers search for the most informative examples in parallel while a single worker updates the model on examples selected by importance sampling, which leads the model to update using an unbiased estimate of the gradient.

core.title: From STDP towards Biologically Plausible Deep Learning
core.summary: Spike-based simulations agree with the proposed relationship between spike timing and the temporal change of postsynaptic activity and show a strong correlation between the biologically observed STDP behavior and the behavior obtained from simulations where the weight change follows the gradient of the predictive objective function.

core.title: Learning to Understand Phrases by Embedding the Dictionary
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work proposes using the definitions found in everyday dictionaries as a means of bridging the gap between lexical and phrasal semantics, and presents two applications of these architectures: reverse dictionaries that return the name of a concept given a definition or description and general-knowledge crossword question answerers.

core.title: Bidirectional Helmholtz Machines
core.summary: A new model is proposed which guarantees that the top-down and bottom-up distributions can efficiently invert each other, and which results in state of the art generative models which prefer significantly deeper architectures while it allows for orders of magnitude more efficient approximate inference.

core.title: Document Analysis with Transducers
core.summary: This architecture generalizes techniques used in Neural Networks, Optical Character Recognition, Natural Language Processing and Speech Recognition and is composed of a succession of modules transforming graphs describing lower-level hypotheses on the documents into graphs describing higher level hypotheses.

core.title: Gated Feedback Recurrent Neural Networks
core.summary: The empirical evaluation of different RNN units revealed that the proposed gated-feedback RNN outperforms the conventional approaches to build deep stacked RNNs in the tasks of character-level language modeling and Python program evaluation.

core.title: Editorial introduction to the Neural Networks special issue on Deep Learning of Representations
ReSeg: A Recurrent Neural Network-Based Model for Semantic Segmentation
core.venue: 2016 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
core.summary: A structured prediction architecture, which exploits the local generic features extracted by Convolutional Neural Networks and the capacity of Recurrent Neural Networks to retrieve distant dependencies, based on the recently introduced ReNet model for image classification is proposed.

core.title: IAPR keynote lecture IV: Deep learning
core.summary: This talk will summarize the advances that have made these breakthroughs possible, and end with questions about some major challenges still ahead of researchers in order to continue the climb towards AI-level competence.

core.title: Early Inference in Energy-Based Models Approximates Back-Propagation
core.summary: It is shown that Langevin MCMC inference in an energy-based model with latent variables has the property that the early steps of inference, starting from a stationary point, correspond to propagating error gradients into internal layers, similarly to back-propagation.

core.title: Blocks and Fuel
Trainable performance upper bounds for image and video captioning
core.summary: This work utilizes existing natural language parsers to extract key concepts from ground truth captions, and establishes empirically dataset-dependent upper bounds on various automatic evaluation metrics commonly used to compare models.

core.title: Unitary Evolution Recurrent Neural Networks
core.summary: This work constructs an expressive unitary weight matrix by composing several structured matrices that act as building blocks with parameters to be learned, and demonstrates the potential of this architecture by achieving state of the art results in several hard tasks involving very long-term dependencies.

core.title: Training Bidirectional Helmholtz Machines
core.summary: This work presents a lower-bound for the likelihood of the generative model and shows that optimizing this bound regularizes the model so that the Bhattacharyya distance between the bottom-up and top-down approximate distributions is minimized.

core.title: Batch normalized recurrent neural networks
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: This paper investigates how batch normalization can be applied to RNNs and shows that the way it is applied leads to a faster convergence of the training criterion but doesn't seem to improve the generalization performance.

core.title: How transferable are features in deep neural networks?
core.summary: This paper quantifies the generality versus specificity of neurons in each layer of a deep convolutional neural network and reports a few surprising results, including that initializing a network with transferred features from almost any number of layers can produce a boost to generalization that lingers even after fine-tuning to the target dataset.

core.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder–Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: Qualitatively, the proposed RNN Encoder‐Decoder model learns a semantically and syntactically meaningful representation of linguistic phrases.

core.title: Supplementary material for : How transferable are features in deep neural networks ?
