core.summary: This study aims not for maximum absolute performance but to use a commonly studied architecture, using the reference implementation provided by Caffe, and uses dropout on fully connected layers except for the softmax output layer.

core.title: Supplemental Material for : Deep Generative Stochastic Networks Trainable by Backprop
core.summary: If Pθn(X) is a consistent estimator of the true conditional distribution P (X|X̃) and Tn defines an ergodic Markov chain, then as n → ∞, the asymptotic distribution πn( X) of the generated samples converges to the data-generating distribution P(X).

core.title: Not All Neural Embeddings are Born Equal
core.summary: It is shown that translation-based embeddings outperform those learned by cutting-edge monolingual models at single-language tasks requiring knowledge of conceptual similarity and/or syntactic role.

core.title: The Spike-and-Slab RBM and Extensions to Discrete and Sparse Data Distributions
core.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

core.title: On Using Very Large Target Vocabulary for Neural Machine Translation
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: It is shown that decoding can be efficiently done even with the model having a very large target vocabulary by selecting only a small subset of the whole target vocabulary.

core.title: Training deep neural networks with low precision multiplications
core.summary: It is found that very low precision is sufficient not just for running trained networks but also for training them, and it is possible to train Maxout networks with 10 bits multiplications.

core.title: On the Properties of Neural Machine Translation: Encoder–Decoder Approaches
core.summary: It is shown that the neural machine translation performs relatively well on short sentences without unknown words, but its performance degrades rapidly as the length of the sentence and the number of unknown words increase.

core.title: Embedding Word Similarity with Neural Machine Translation
core.summary: Embeddings from translation models outperform those learned by monolingual models at tasks that require knowledge of both conceptual similarity and lexical-syntactic role, and are indicated that translation-based embeddings should be used in applications that require concepts to be organised according to similarity and/or lexical function.

core.title: End-to-end Continuous Speech Recognition using Attention-based Recurrent NN: First Results
core.summary: Initial results demonstrate that this new approach achieves phoneme error rates that are comparable to the state-of-the-art HMM-based decoders, on the TIMIT dataset.

core.title: Deep learning and cultural evolution
core.venue: Annual Conference on Genetic and Evolutionary Computation
core.summary: A theory and its first experimental tests are proposed, relating difficulty of learning in deep architectures to culture and language and an empirical test of the hypothesis regarding the need for guidance of intermediate concepts is demonstrated.

core.title: Ensemble of Generative and Discriminative Techniques for Sentiment Analysis of Movie Reviews
core.summary: This work shows how to use for this task the standard generative models, which are slightly complementary to the state of the art techniques, and achieves strong results on a well-known dataset of IMDB movie reviews.

core.title: Evolving Culture Versus Local Minima
core.summary: It is implied that human culture and the evolution of ideas have been crucial to counter an optimization difficulty that would otherwise make it very difficult for human brains to capture high-level knowledge of the world.

core.title: Overcoming the Curse of Sentence Length for Neural Machine Translation using Automatic Segmentation
core.summary: A way to address the issue of a significant drop in translation quality when translating long sentences by automatically segmenting an input sentence into phrases that can be easily translated by the neural network translation model.

core.title: Learning semantic representations of objects and their parts
core.summary: This paper designs a model architecture that can be trained under a proxy supervision obtained by combining standard image annotation with semantic part-based within-label relations (from WordNet), and is designed to model both object image to object label similarities, and object label to object part label similarities in a single joint system.

core.title: Reweighted Wake-Sleep
core.summary: A novel interpretation of the wake-sleep algorithm is proposed which suggests that better estimators of the gradient can be obtained by sampling latent variables multiple times from the inference network, and using a more powerful layer model, such as NADE, yields substantially better generative models.

core.title: Learning Concept Embeddings for Query Expansion by Quantum Entropy Minimization
core.summary: A novel method for learning, in a supervised way, semantic representations for words and phrases by embedding queries and documents in special matrices, which disposes of an increased representational power with respect to existing approaches adopting a vector representation.

core.title: How Auto-Encoders Could Provide Credit Assignment in Deep Networks via Target Propagation
core.summary: The motivations and theoretical justifications for this approach are laid down, along with conjectures that will have to be verified either mathematically or experimentally, including a hypothesis stating that such auto-encoder mediated target propagation could play in brains the role of credit assignment through many non-linear, noisy and discrete transformations.

core.title: Low precision storage for deep learning
core.summary: It is found that very low precision storage is sufficient not just for running trained networks but also for training them.

core.title: FitNets: Hints for Thin Deep Nets
core.summary: This paper extends the idea of a student network that could imitate the soft output of a larger teacher network or ensemble of networks, using not only the outputs but also the intermediate representations learned by the teacher as hints to improve the training process and final performance of the student.

core.title: On the saddle point problem for non-convex optimization
core.summary: It is argued, based on results from statistical physics, random matrix theory, and neural network theory, that a deeper and more profound difficulty originates from the proliferation of saddle points, not local minima, especially in high dimensional problems of practical interest.

core.title: Deep Tempering
core.summary: This work proposes a novel method of sampling from Boltzmann machines that demonstrates a computationally efficient way to promote mixing and leverages an under-appreciated property of deep generative models such as the Deep Belief Network (DBN).

core.title: Identifying and attacking the saddle point problem in high-dimensional non-convex optimization
core.summary: This paper proposes a new approach to second-order optimization, the saddle-free Newton method, that can rapidly escape high dimensional saddle points, unlike gradient descent and quasi-Newton methods, and applies this algorithm to deep or recurrent neural network training, and provides numerical evidence for its superior optimization performance.

core.title: Empirical Evaluation of Gated Recurrent Neural Networks on Sequence Modeling
core.summary: These advanced recurrent units that implement a gating mechanism, such as a long short-term memory (LSTM) unit and a recently proposed gated recurrent unit (GRU), are found to be comparable to LSTM.

core.title: On the Number of Linear Regions of Deep Neural Networks
core.summary: The complexity of functions computable by deep feedforward neural networks with piecewise linear activations in terms of the symmetries and the number of linear regions that they have is investigated.

core.title: Deep Directed Generative Autoencoders
core.summary: Although optimizing a single level of such architecture may be difficult, much better results can be obtained by pre-training and stacking them, gradually transforming the data distribution into one that is more easily captured by a simple parametric model.

core.title: ADASECANT: Robust Adaptive Secant Method for Stochastic Gradient
core.summary: A new adaptive learning rate algorithm, which utilizes curvature information for automatically tuning the learning rates and a new variance reduction technique to speed up the convergence of SGD.

core.title: Difference Target Propagation
core.summary: It is shown that a linear correction for the imperfectness of the auto-encoders, called difference target propagation, is very effective to make target propagation actually work, leading to results comparable to back-propagation for deep networks with discrete and continuous units and denoising auto- encoders and achieving state of the art for stochastic networks.

core.title: Iterative Neural Autoregressive Distribution Estimator NADE-k
core.summary: The proposed NADE-k is an unsupervised building block for deep learning that combines the desirable properties of NADE and multi-prediction training and uses an inference engine that is a superset of variational inference for Boltzmann machines.

core.title: Scaling up deep learning
core.summary: This tutorial will introduce some of the basic algorithms, both on the supervised and unsupervised sides, as well as discuss some ofThe guidelines for successfully using them in practice, and introduces current research questions regarding the challenge of scaling up deep learning to much larger models that can successfully extract information from huge datasets.

core.title: Exponentially Increasing the Capacity-to-Computation Ratio for Conditional Computation in Deep Learning
core.summary: A novel parametrization of weight matrices in neural networks which has the potential to increase up to exponentially the ratio of the number of parameters to computation is proposed, which is based on turning on some parameters (weight matrices) when specific bit patterns of hidden unit activations are obtained.

core.title: Low precision arithmetic for deep learning
core.summary: It is found that very low precision computation is sufficient not just for running trained networks but also for training them.

core.title: NICE: Non-linear Independent Components Estimation
core.summary: A deep learning framework for modeling complex high-dimensional densities called Non-linear Independent Component Estimation (NICE) is proposed, based on the idea that a good representation is one in which the data has a distribution that is easy to model.

core.title: Marginalized Denoising Auto-encoders for Nonlinear Representations
core.summary: The marginalized Denoising Auto-encoder (mDAE) is presented, which (approximately) marginalizes out the corruption during training and is able to match or outperform the DAE with much fewer training epochs.

core.title: On the Equivalence between Deep NADE and Generative Stochastic Networks
core.summary: This work shows an alternative way to sample from a trained Orderless NADE that allows to trade-off computing time and quality of the samples, and makes a connection between this criterion and the training criterion for Generative Stochastic Networks (GSNs).

core.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
core.summary: It is conjecture that the use of a fixed-length vector is a bottleneck in improving the performance of this basic encoder-decoder architecture, and it is proposed to extend this by allowing a model to automatically (soft-)search for parts of a source sentence that are relevant to predicting a target word, without having to form these parts as a hard segment explicitly.

core.title: BilBOWA: Fast Bilingual Distributed Representations without Word Alignments
core.summary: It is shown that bilingual embeddings learned using the proposed BilBOWA model outperform state-of-the-art methods on a cross-lingual document classification task as well as a lexical translation task on WMT11 data.

core.title: Deep Learning of Representations
core.summary: This chapter reviews the main motivations and ideas behind deep learning algorithms and their representation-learning components, as well as recent results, and proposes a vision of challenges and hopes on the road ahead, focusing on the questions of invariance and disentangling.

core.title: An Empirical Investigation of Catastrophic Forgeting in Gradient-Based Neural Networks
core.summary: It is found that it is always best to train using the dropout algorithm--the drop out algorithm is consistently best at adapting to the new task, remembering the old task, and has the best tradeoff curve between these two extremes.

core.title: Unsupervised and Transfer Learning under Uncertainty - From Object Detections to Scene Categorization
core.venue: International Conference on Pattern Recognition Applications and Methods
core.summary: This paper uses the features provided by Object-Bank (Li-Jia Li and Fei-Fei, 2010a) and shows that careful combinations, taking into account the structure of the data, allows to greatly improve over original results.

core.title: Stacked calibration of off-policy policy evaluation for video game matchmaking
core.venue: IEEE Conference on Computational Intelligence and Games

core.title: Learned-Norm Pooling for Deep Feedforward and Recurrent Neural Networks
core.summary: It is shown that multilayer perceptrons (MLP) consisting of the L p units achieve the state-of-the-art results on a number of benchmark datasets and the proposed L p unit is evaluated on the recently proposed deep recurrent neural networks (RNN).

core.title: On the Challenges of Physical Implementations of RBMs
core.summary: This work conducts software simulations to determine how harmful each of the topology restrictions of currently existing physical computers are and suggests that designers of new physical computing hardware and algorithms for physical computers should focus their efforts on overcoming them.

core.title: Multimodal Transitions for Generative Stochastic Networks
core.summary: This work introduces for the first time multimodal transition distributions for GSNs, in particular using models in the NADE family (Neural Autoregressive Density Estimator) as output distributions of the transition operator.

core.title: Pylearn2: a machine learning research library
core.summary: A brief history of the library, an overview of its basic philosophy, a summary of the Library's architecture, and a description of how the Pylearn2 community functions socially are given.

core.title: Big Neural Networks Waste Capacity
core.summary: The experiments on ImageNet LSVRC-2010 show that this may be due to the fact there are highly diminishing returns for capacity in terms of training error, leading to underfitting, suggesting that the optimization method - first order gradient descent - fails at this regime.

core.title: Estimating or Propagating Gradients Through Stochastic Neurons
core.summary: It is demonstrated that a simple biologically plausible formula gives rise to an an unbiased (but noisy) estimator of the gradient with respect to a binary stochastic neuron firing proba bility, and an approach to approximating this unbiased but high-variance estimator by learning to predict it using a biased estimator.

core.title: Learning deep physiological models of affect
Scaling Up Spike-and-Slab Models for Unsupervised Feature Learning
core.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

core.title: Combining modality specific deep neural networks for emotion recognition in video
core.summary: This paper presents the techniques used for the University of Montréal's team submissions to the 2013 Emotion Recognition in the Wild Challenge, a challenge to classify the emotions expressed by the primary human subject in short video clips extracted from feature length movies.

core.title: Knowledge Matters: Importance of Prior Information for Optimization
core.summary: The effect of introducing prior information into the intermediate level of neural networks for a learning task on which all the state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms tested failed to learn is explored.

core.title: How to Construct Deep Recurrent Neural Networks
core.summary: Two novel architectures of a deep RNN are proposed which are orthogonal to an earlier attempt of stacking multiple recurrent layers to build aDeep RNN, and an alternative interpretation is provided using a novel framework based on neural operators.

core.title: Multi-Prediction Deep Boltzmann Machines
core.summary: The multi-prediction deep Boltzmann machine does not require greedy layerwise pretraining, and outperforms the standard DBM at classification, classification with missing inputs, and mean field prediction tasks.

core.title: Deep Learning for NLP (without Magic)
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: The principle goal of the tutorial is to make the inner workings of these techniques transparent, intuitive and their results interpretable, rather than black boxes labeled ”magic here”.

core.title: Bounding the Test Log-Likelihood of Generative Models
core.summary: A more efficient estimator is proposed, and it is proved that it provides a lower bound on the true test log-likelihood, and an unbiased estimator as the number of generated samples goes to infinity, although one that incorporates the effect of poor mixing.

core.title: Deep Generative Stochastic Networks Trainable by Backprop
core.summary: Theorems that generalize recent work on the probabilistic interpretation of denoising autoencoders are provided and obtain along the way an interesting justification for dependency networks and generalized pseudolikelihood.

core.title: Estimating or Propagating Gradients Through Stochastic Neurons for Conditional Computation
core.summary: This work considers a small-scale version of {\em conditional computation}, where sparse stochastic units form a distributed representation of gaters that can turn off in combinatorially many ways large chunks of the computation performed in the rest of the neural network.

core.title: Learned-norm pooling for deep neural networks
An empirical analysis of dropout in piecewise linear networks
core.summary: This work empirically investigate several questions related to the efficacy of dropout, specifically as it concerns networks employing the popular rectified linear activation function, and investigates an alternative criterion based on a biased estimator of the maximum likelihood ensemble gradient.

core.title: Deep Learning of Representations: Looking Forward
core.venue: International Conference on Statistical Language and Speech Processing
core.summary: This paper proposes to examine some of the challenges of scaling deep learning algorithms to much larger models and datasets, reducing optimization difficulties due to ill-conditioning or local minima, designing more efficient and powerful inference and sampling procedures, and learning to disentangle the factors of variation underlying the observed data.

core.title: Joint Training Deep Boltzmann Machines for Classification
core.summary: This work introduces a new method for training deep Boltzmann machines jointly, and shows that this approach performs competitively for classification and outperforms previous methods in terms of accuracy of approximate inference and classification with missing inputs.

core.title: Statistical Language and Speech Processing
core.summary: This paper proposes to examine some of the challenges of scaling deep learning algorithms to much larger models and datasets, reducing optimization difficulties due to ill-conditioning or local minima, designing more efficient and powerful inference and sampling procedures, and learning to disentangle the factors of variation underlying the observed data.

core.title: Conditioning and time representation in long short-term memory networks
core.summary: It is shown that it is possible, with the proposed architecture, to acquire discharge patterns similar to those observed in dopaminergic neurons and in the cerebral cortex on those tasks simply by minimizing a predictive cost function.

core.title: Metric-Free Natural Gradient for Joint-Training of Boltzmann Machines
core.summary: The Metric-Free Natural Gradient algorithm is introduced and it is shown that MFNG does indeed have faster per-epoch convergence compared to Stochastic Maximum Likelihood with centering, though wall-clock performance is currently not competitive.

core.title: Modeling term dependencies with quantum language models for IR
core.venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
core.summary: This work develops a new, generalized Language Modeling approach for IR by adopting the probabilistic framework of QT, which is the first practical application of quantum probability to show significant improvements over a robust bag-of-words baseline and achieves better performance on a stronger non bag- of- words baseline.

core.title: Estimating Car Insuran e Premia : a Case Study in High-Dimensional
Maxout Networks
core.summary: A simple new model called maxout is defined designed to both facilitate optimization by dropout and improve the accuracy of dropout's fast approximate model averaging technique.

core.title: On the number of inference regions of deep feed forward networks with piece-wise linear activations
core.summary: This paper offers a framework for comparing deep and shallow models that belong to the family of piecewise linear functions based on computational geometry and looks at a deep rectifier multi-layer perceptron (MLP) with linear outputs units and compares it with a single layer version of the model.

core.title: Natural Gradient Revisited
Investigation of recurrent-neural-network architectures and learning methods for spoken language understanding
core.summary: The results show that on this task, both types of recurrent networks outperform the CRF baseline substantially, and a bi-directional Jordantype network that takes into account both past and future dependencies among slots works best, outperforming a CRFbased baseline by 14% in relative error reduction.

core.title: Stochastic Ratio Matching of RBMs for Sparse High-Dimensional Inputs
core.summary: It is shown that stochastic ratio matching is a good estimator, allowing the approach to beat the state-of-the-art on two bag- of-word text classification benchmarks (20 Newsgroups and RCV1), while keeping computational cost linear in the number of non-zeros.

core.title: On the number of response regions of deep feed forward networks with piece-wise linear activations
core.summary: This paper offers a framework for comparing deep and shallow models that belong to the family of piecewise linear functions based on computational geometry, and looks at a deep rectifier multi-layer perceptron with linear outputs units and compares it with a single layer version of the model.

core.title: Generalized Denoising Auto-Encoders as Generative Models
core.summary: A different attack on the problem is proposed, which deals with arbitrary (but noisy enough) corruption, arbitrary reconstruction loss, handling both discrete and continuous-valued variables, and removing the bias due to non-infinitesimal corruption noise.

core.title: Challenges in representation learning: A report on three machine learning contests
core.summary: The datasets created for these challenges are described, the results of the competitions are summarized, and some comments are provided on what kind of knowledge can be gained from machine learning competitions.

core.title: Audio Chord Recognition with Recurrent Neural Networks
core.venue: International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference
core.summary: An efficient algorithm to search for the global mode of the output distribution while taking long-term dependencies into account is devised and the resulting method is competitive with state-of-the-art approaches on the MIREX dataset in the major/minor prediction task.

core.title: Unsupervised Learning of Semantics of Object Detections for Scene Categorization
core.venue: International Conference on Pattern Recognition Applications and Methods
core.summary: This paper uses the features provided by Object-Bank, and shows that careful combinations, taking into account the structure of the data, allows to greatly improve over original results, while drastically reducing the dimensionality of the representation by 97 %.

core.title: Revisiting Natural Gradient for Deep Networks
core.summary: It is described how one can use unlabeled data to improve the generalization error obtained by natural gradient and empirically evaluate the robustness of the algorithm to the ordering of the training set compared to stochastic gradient descent.

core.title: A semantic matching energy function for learning with multi-relational data
core.summary: A new neural network architecture designed to embed multi-relational graphs into a flexible continuous vector space in which the original data is kept and enhanced, demonstrating that it can scale up to tens of thousands of nodes and thousands of types of relation.

core.title: J un 2 01 3 Deep Learning of Representations : Looking Forward
core.summary: This paper proposes to examine some of the challenges of scaling deep learning algorithms to much larger models and datasets, reducing optimization difficulties due to ill-conditioning or local minima, designing more efficient and powerful inference and sampling procedures, and learning to disentangle the factors of variation underlying the observed data.

core.title: Deep Learning for NLP (without Magic) References
core.summary: A framework for learning predictive structures from multiple tasks and unlabeled data and a neural probabilistic language model for this framework are presented.

core.title: Modeling Temporal Dependencies in High-Dimensional Sequences: Application to Polyphonic Music Generation and Transcription
core.summary: A probabilistic model based on distribution estimators conditioned on a recurrent neural network that is able to discover temporal dependencies in high-dimensional sequences that outperforms many traditional models of polyphonic music on a variety of realistic datasets is introduced.

core.title: Learning Algorithms for the Classification Restricted Boltzmann Machine
core.summary: It is argued that RBMs can provide a self-contained framework for developing competitive classifiers and it is shown that competitive classification performances can be reached when appropriately combining discriminative and generative training objectives.

core.title: Large-Scale Feature Learning With Spike-and-Slab Sparse Coding
core.summary: This work introduces a new feature learning and extraction procedure based on a factor model the authors call spike-and-slab sparse coding (S3C), and presents a novel inference procedure for appropriate for use with GPUs which allows to dramatically increase both the training set size and the amount of latent factors that S3C may be trained with.

core.title: Representation Learning: A Review and New Perspectives
core.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
core.summary: Recent work in the area of unsupervised feature learning and deep learning is reviewed, covering advances in probabilistic models, autoencoders, manifold learning, and deep networks.

core.title: Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization
core.summary: This paper shows empirically and theoretically that randomly chosen trials are more efficient for hyper-parameter optimization than trials on a grid, and shows that random search is a natural baseline against which to judge progress in the development of adaptive (sequential) hyper- parameter optimization algorithms.

core.title: Building Musically-relevant Audio Features through Multiple Timescale Representations
core.venue: International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference
core.summary: A method to obtain multi-scale features of music audio such as melody, harmony, phrasing and rhythm and its effectiveness for automatic tag annotation is described and evaluated.

core.title: A Generative Process for Contractive Auto-Encoders.
core.summary: A procedure for generating samples that are consistent with the local structure captured by a contractive auto-encoder and which experimentally appears to converge quickly and mix well between modes, compared to Restricted Boltzmann Machines and Deep Belief Networks is proposed.

core.title: What regularized auto-encoders learn from the data-generating distribution
core.summary: It is shown that the auto-encoder captures the score (derivative of the log-density with respect to the input) and contradicts previous interpretations of reconstruction error as an energy function.

core.title: Theano: Deep Learning on GPUs with Python
core.summary: This paper presents Theano, a framework in the Python programming language for defining, optimizing and evaluating expressions involving high-level operations on tensors, and adds automatic symbolic differentiation, GPU support, and faster expression evaluation.

core.title: Beyond Skill Rating: Advanced Matchmaking in Ghost Recon Online
core.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Intelligence and AI in Games

core.title: On Training Deep Boltzmann Machines
core.summary: A simple regularization scheme is introduced that encourages the weight vectors associated with each hidden unit to have similar norms and can be easily combined with standard stochastic maximum likelihood to yield an effective training strategy for the simultaneous training of all layers of the deep Boltzmann machine.

core.title: Practical Recommendations for Gradient-Based Training of Deep Architectures
core.summary: Overall, this chapter describes elements of the practice used to successfully and efficiently train and debug large-scale and often deep multi-layer neural networks and closes with open questions about the training difficulties observed with deeper architectures.

core.title: Regularized Auto-Encoders Estimate Local Statistics
core.summary: It is shown that minimizing a particular form of regularized reconstruction error yields a reconstruction function that locally characterizes the shape of the data generating density.

core.title: Disentangling Factors of Variation via Generative Entangling
core.summary: This work proposes a novel model family based on the spike-and-slab restricted Boltzmann machine which is generalize to include higher-order interactions among multiple latent variables and applies it to the task of facial expression classification.

core.title: Evolving Culture vs Local Minima
core.summary: It is implied that human culture and the evolution of ideas have been crucial to counter an optimization difficulty that would otherwise make it very difficult for human brains to capture high-level knowledge of the world.

core.title: A Generative Process for Contractive Auto-Encoders
core.summary: A procedure for generating samples that are consistent with the local structure captured by a contractive auto-encoder and which experimentally appears to converge quickly and mix well between modes, compared to Restricted Boltzmann Machines and Deep Belief Networks is proposed.

core.title: Discriminative Non-negative Matrix Factorization for Multiple Pitch Estimation
core.venue: International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference
core.summary: The idea is to extend the sparse NMF framework by incorporating pitch information present in time-aligned musical scores in order to extract features that enforce the separability between pitch labels.

core.title: Deep Learning for Automatic Summary Scoring
core.summary: A new approach based on representation learning, using both unsupervised and supervised learning components, to score a summary based on examples of manually evaluated summaries, greatly surpassed ROUGE in terms of correlation with Pyramid (content) scores for individual summaries.

core.title: Apprentissage machine efficace: theorie et pratique
core.summary: It is proved that using networks with a single hidden layer can be exponentially less efficient than when using deep networks, and analyses help better understand some inherent flaws found in existing algorithms, and steer research towards approaches that may potentially overcome them.

core.title: Efficient EM Training of Gaussian Mixtures with Missing Data
core.summary: This paper introduces a spanning-tree based algorithm that significantly speeds up training in these conditions of data-mining applications and observes that good results can be obtained by using the generative model to fill-in the missing values for a separate discriminant learning algorithm.

core.title: On the difficulty of training recurrent neural networks
core.summary: This paper proposes a gradient norm clipping strategy to deal with exploding gradients and a soft constraint for the vanishing gradients problem and validates empirically the hypothesis and proposed solutions.

core.title: Theano: new features and speed improvements
core.summary: New features and efficiency improvements to Theano are presented, and benchmarks demonstrating Theano's performance relative to Torch7, a recently introduced machine learning library, and to RNNLM, a C++ library targeted at recurrent neural networks.

core.title: High-dimensional sequence transduction
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: A probabilistic model based on a recurrent neural network that is able to learn realistic output distributions given the input is introduced and an efficient algorithm to search for the global mode of that distribution is devised.

core.title: Spike-and-Slab Sparse Coding for Unsupervised Feature Discovery
core.summary: This work derives a structured variational inference procedure and employs a variational EM training algorithm to improve upon the supervised learning capabilities of both sparse coding and the ssRBM on the CIFAR-10 dataset.

core.title: Joint Training of Deep Boltzmann Machines
core.summary: A new method for training deep Boltzmann machines jointly is introduced that requires an initial learning pass that trains the deep BoltZmann machine greedily, one layer at a time, or do not perform well on classifi- cation tasks.

core.title: Understanding the exploding gradient problem
core.summary: The analysis is used to justify the simple yet effective solution of norm clipping the exploded gradient, and the comparison between this heuristic solution and standard SGD provides empirical evidence towards the hypothesis that such a heuristic is required to reach state of the art results on a character prediction task and a polyphonic music prediction one.

core.title: Better Mixing via Deep Representations
core.summary: It is proposed that the higher-level samples fill more uniformly the space they occupy and the high-density manifolds tend to unfold when represented at higher levels, and mixing between modes would be more efficient at higher Levels of representation.

core.title: Advances in optimizing recurrent networks
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.summary: Experiments reported here evaluate the use of clipping gradients, spanning longer time ranges with leaky integration, advanced momentum techniques, using more powerful output probability models, and encouraging sparser gradients to help symmetry breaking and credit assignment.

core.title: DETONATION CLASSIFICATION FROM ACOUSTIC SIGNATURE WITH THE RESTRICTED BOLTZMANN MACHINE
core.summary: Experiments show good classification accuracy that could make these techniques suitable for fielding on autonomous devices, and DRBMs appear to yield better accuracy than SVMs, and are less sensitive to the choice of signal preprocessing and model hyperparameters.

core.title: Implicit Density Estimation by Local Moment Matching to Sample from Auto-Encoders
core.summary: A contribution of this work is a novel alternative to maximum-likelihood density estimation, which is local moment matching, which justifies a recently proposed sampling algorithm for the Contractive Auto-Encoder and extends it to the Denoising Auto- Encoder.

core.title: Joint Learning of Words and Meaning Representations for Open-Text Semantic Parsing
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: This work proposes a method that learns to assign MRs to a wide range of text thanks to a training scheme that combines learning from knowledge bases with learning from raw text.

core.title: Texture Modeling with Convolutional Spike-and-Slab RBMs and Deep Extensions
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: The resulting deep belief network (DBN) is a powerful generative model that improves on single-layer models and is capable of modeling not only single high-resolution and challenging textures but also multiple textures.

core.title: Unsupervised Feature Learning and Deep Learning: A Review and New Perspectives
core.summary: Recent work in the area of unsupervised feature learning and deep learning is reviewed, covering advances in probabilistic models, manifold learning, and deep learning.

core.title: Disentangling Factors of Variation for Facial Expression Recognition
core.summary: A semi-supervised approach to solve the task of emotion recognition in 2D face images using recent ideas in deep learning for handling the factors of variation present in data, beating the state-of-the-art on a recently proposed dataset for facial expression recognition.

core.title: Algorithms for Hyper-Parameter Optimization
core.summary: This work contributes novel techniques for making response surface models P(y|x) in which many elements of hyper-parameter assignment (x) are known to be irrelevant given particular values of other elements.

core.title: Learning invariant features through local space contraction
core.summary: A novel approach for training deterministic auto-encoders is presented that by adding a well chosen penalty term to the classical reconstruction cost function, it is shown that this penalty term results in a localized space contraction which in turn yields robust features on the activation layer.

core.title: On learning distributed representations of semantics
core.venue: Symposium on Machine Learning in Speech and Language Processing

core.title: Contractive Auto-Encoders: Explicit Invariance During Feature Extraction
core.summary: It is found empirically that this penalty helps to carve a representation that better captures the local directions of variation dictated by the data, corresponding to a lower-dimensional non-linear manifold, while being more invariant to the vast majority of directions orthogonal to the manifold.

core.title: Mining
Learning Structured Embeddings of Knowledge Bases
core.summary: A learning process based on an innovative neural network architecture designed to embed any of these symbolic representations into a more flexible continuous vector space in which the original knowledge is kept and enhanced would allow data from any KB to be easily used in recent machine learning meth- ods for prediction and information retrieval.

core.title: Higher Order Contractive Auto-Encoder
core.summary: A novel regularizer when training an autoencoder for unsupervised feature extraction yields representations that are significantly better suited for initializing deep architectures than previously proposed approaches, beating state-of-the-art performance on a number of datasets.

core.title: On Tracking The Partition Function
core.summary: This paper exploits the gradient descent training procedure of restricted Boltzmann machines (a type of MRF) to track the log partition function during learning, and provides this estimate at each time-step, at a computational cost similar to that required for training alone.

core.title: Contextual tag inference
core.summary: It is shown that users agree more on tags applied to clips temporally “closer” to one another; that conditional restricted Boltzmann machine models of tags can more accurately predict related tags when they take context into account; and that when training data is “smoothed” using context, support vector machines can better rank these clips according to the original, unsmoothed tags.

core.title: Deep Learners Benefit More from Out-of-Distribution Examples
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: Results show that a deep learner did beat previously published results and reached human-level performance, and the hypothesis is that intermediate levels of representation, because they can be shared across tasks and examples from different but related distributions, can yield even more benefits.

core.title: Adding noise to the input of a model trained with a regularized objective
core.summary: This work derives the higher order terms of the Taylor expansion and analyzes the coefficients of the regularization terms induced by the noisy input of a parametric function to study the effect of penalizing the Hessian of the mapping function with respect to the input in terms of generalization performance.

core.title: Shallow vs. Deep Sum-Product Networks
core.summary: It is proved there exist families of functions that can be represented much more efficiently with a deep network than with a shallow one, i.e. with substantially fewer hidden units.

core.title: Understanding deep architectures and the effect of unsupervised pre-training
core.summary: It is argued that models that are based on a shallow composition of local features are not appropriate for the set of real-world functions and datasets that are of interest to us, namely data with many factors of variation.

core.title: Unsupervised Models of Images by Spikeand-Slab RBMs
core.summary: This paper generalizes and extends the spike-and-slab RBM to include non-zero means of the conditional distribution over the observed variables given the binary spike variables, and introduces a term, quadratic in the observed data that is exploited to guarantee that all conditionals associated with the model are well defined.

core.title: Discussion of "The Neural Autoregressive Distribution Estimator"
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: The Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) is an undirected graphical model with latent variables, exact inference, rather simple sampling procedures (block Gibbs), and several successful learning algorithms based on approximations of the log-likelihood gradient.

core.title: Deep Sparse Rectifier Neural Networks
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: This paper shows that rectifying neurons are an even better model of biological neurons and yield equal or better performance than hyperbolic tangent networks in spite of the hard non-linearity and non-dierentiabil ity.

core.title: Autotagging music with conditional restricted Boltzmann machines
core.summary: This paper describes two applications of conditional restricted Boltzmann machines (CRBMs) to the task of autotagging music, and the use of a discriminative RBM, a type of CRBM, to autotag music.

core.title: An Energy-Based Recurrent Neural Network for Multiple Fundamental Frequency Estimation
core.summary: The Recurrent TRBM (RTRBM) is a slight modification of the TRBM that allows for exact inference and efficient training by contrastive divergence (CD) and can be understood as a sequence of RBMs whose parameters are understood.

core.title: Domain Adaptation for Large-Scale Sentiment Classification: A Deep Learning Approach
core.summary: A deep learning approach is proposed which learns to extract a meaningful representation for each review in an unsupervised fashion and clearly outperform state-of-the-art methods on a benchmark composed of reviews of 4 types of Amazon products.

core.title: A Spike and Slab Restricted Boltzmann Machine
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: The spike and slab Restricted Boltzmann Machine is introduced, characterized by having both a real-valued vector, the slab, and a binary variable, the spike, associated with each unit in the hidden layer.

core.title: The Manifold Tangent Classifier
core.summary: A representation learning algorithm can be stacked to yield a deep architecture and it is shown how it builds a topological atlas of charts, each chart being characterized by the principal singular vectors of the Jacobian of a representation mapping.

core.title: Towards Open-Text Semantic Parsing via Multi-Task Learning of Structured Embeddings
core.summary: This work proposes a method that learns to assign MRs to a wide range of text thanks to a training scheme that combines learning from WordNet and ConceptNet with learning from raw text.

core.title: On the Expressive Power of Deep Architectures
core.venue: International Conference on Algorithmic Learning Theory
core.summary: Some of the theoretical motivations for deep architectures, as well as some of their practical successes, are reviewed, and directions of investigations to address some of the remaining challenges are proposed.

core.title: The Statistical Inefficiency of Sparse Coding for Images (or, One Gabor to Rule them All)
core.summary: There is so much redundancy in sparse codes for natural images that the model requires only a single dictionary element (a Gabor-like edge detector) to outperform standard sparse coding, and the model scales naturally to arbitrary-sized images while achieving much greater statistical efficiency during learning.

core.title: Suitability of V1 Energy Models for Object Classification
core.summary: This work finds that complex cell rate models learn to categorize objects better than simple cell models, and without incurring extra computational expense, and finds that the squaring of linear filter responses leads to better performance.

core.title: A Common GPU n-Dimensional Array for Python and C
core.summary: This paper proposes and presents a first version of a common GPU n-dimensional array (tensor) named GpuNdArray that works with both CUDA and OpenCL and will be usable from Python, C, and possibly other programming languages.

core.title: Adaptive Drift-Diffusion Process to Learn Time Intervals
core.summary: A new model of interval timing is presented, based on simple temporal integrators, derived from drift-diffusion models, that can learn inter-event intervals in a number of trials independent of the interval size and that the temporal precision of the system is proportional to the timed interval.

core.title: Large-Scale Learning of Embeddings with Reconstruction Sampling
core.summary: A novel method to speed up the learning of embeddings for large-scale learning tasks involving very sparse data, as is typically the case for Natural Language Processing tasks, using a new method to approximate reconstruction error by a sampling procedure.

core.title: Incorporating complex cells into neural networks for pattern classification
core.summary: The work presented here uses image classification performance (accurate discrimination between common classes of objects) as a basis for comparing visual system models, and algorithms for fitting those models as probability densities to images, and finds that models based on visual area V1's complex cells generalize better from labeled training examples than conventional neural networks whose hidden units are more like V 1's simple cells.

core.title: Quickly Generating Representative Samples from an RBM-Derived Process
core.summary: This work extends FPCD using an idea borrowed from Herding in order to obtain a pure sampling algorithm, which it is called the rates-FPCD sampler, which can improve the model as the authors collect more samples, since it optimizes a lower bound on the log likelihood of the training data.

core.title: Temporal Pooling and Multiscale Learning for Automatic Annotation and Ranking of Music Audio
core.venue: International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference
core.summary: This paper analyzes some of the challenges in performing automatic annotation and ranking of music audio, and proposes a few improvements, including the use of principal component analysis on the mel-scaled spectrum and the idea of multiscale learning.

core.title: Understanding Representations Learned in Deep Architectures
Why Does Unsupervised Pre-training Help Deep Learning?
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: The results suggest that unsupervised pre-training guides the learning towards basins of attraction of minima that support better generalization from the training data set; the evidence from these results supports a regularization explanation for the effect of pre- training.

core.title: Learning Tags that Vary Within a Song
core.venue: International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference
core.summary: It is found that the agreement between different people’s tags decreases as the distance between the parts of a song that they heard increases, and a conditional restricted Boltzmann machine is described to model this relationship.

core.title: Improving First and Second-Order Methods by Modeling Uncertainty
Adaptive Parallel Tempering for Stochastic Maximum Likelihood Learning of RBMs
core.summary: This paper shows that the choice of optimal temperatures can be automated by minimizing average return time while chains can be spawned dynamically, as needed, thus minimizing the computational overhead, and results in better likelihood scores.

core.title: Tractable Multivariate Binary Density Estimation and the Restricted Boltzmann Forest
core.summary: This work argues that for the problem of tractable density estimation, the restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) provides a competitive framework for multivariate binary density modeling and presents the restricted Bolzmann forest (RBForest), which replaces the binary variables in the hidden layer of RBMs with groups of tree-structured binary variables.

core.title: Deep Belief Networks Are Compact Universal Approximators
core.summary: It is proved that deep but narrow feedforward neural networks with sigmoidal units can represent any Boolean expression.

core.title: Theano: A CPU and GPU Math Compiler in Python
core.summary: This paper illustrates how to use Theano, outlines the scope of the compiler, provides benchmarks on both CPU and GPU processors, and explains its overall design.

core.title: Tempered Markov Chain Monte Carlo for training of Restricted Boltzmann Machines
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: This work explores the use of tempered Markov Chain Monte-Carlo for sampling in RBMs and finds both through visualization of samples and measures of likelihood that it helps both sampling and learning.

core.title: Word Representations: A Simple and General Method for Semi-Supervised Learning
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work evaluates Brown clusters, Collobert and Weston (2008) embeddings, and HLBL (Mnih & Hinton, 2009) embeds of words on both NER and chunking, and finds that each of the three word representations improves the accuracy of these baselines.

core.title: Marathi Handwritten Numeral Recognition using Fourier Descriptors and Normalized Chain Code
core.summary: A novel method for automatic recognition of isolated Marathi handwritten numerals using chain code and Fourier Descriptors that capture the information about the shape of the numeral are used as features.

core.title: A simple and general method for semi-supervised learning
core.summary: This work evaluates Brown clusters, Collobert and Weston (2008) embeddings, and HLBL (Mnih & Hinton, 2009) embeds of words on both NER and chunking, and finds that each of the three word representations improves the accuracy of these baselines.

core.title: DECISION TREES DO NOT GENERALIZE TO NEW VARIATIONS
core.summary: It is demonstrated formally that decision trees can be seriously hurt by the curse of dimensionality in a sense that is a bit different from other nonparametric statistical methods, but most importantly that they cannot generalize to variations not seen in the training set.

core.title: Parallel Tempering for Training of Restricted Boltzmann Machines
core.summary: This work explores the use of tempered Markov Chain Monte-Carlo for sampling in RBMs and finds both through visualization of samples and measures of likelihood on a toy dataset that it helps both sampling and learning.

core.title: Modeling Natural Image Covariance with a Spike and Slab Restricted Boltzmann Machine
core.summary: The spike and slab RBM is introduced and it is argued that in the context of latent variable models, the emphasis placed on explicit modeling of covariance versus explicit models of the predicted mean may be somewhat misplaced.

core.title: Stacked Denoising Autoencoders: Learning Useful Representations in a Deep Network with a Local Denoising Criterion
core.summary: This work clearly establishes the value of using a denoising criterion as a tractable unsupervised objective to guide the learning of useful higher level representations.

core.title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: The objective here is to understand better why standard gradient descent from random initialization is doing so poorly with deep neural networks, to better understand these recent relative successes and help design better algorithms in the future.

core.title: Deep Self-Taught Learning for Handwritten Character Recognition
core.summary: It is shown that deep learners benefit more from out-of-distribution examples than a corresponding shallow learner, at least in the area of handwritten character recognition.

core.title: Slow, Decorrelated Features for Pretraining Complex Cell-like Networks
core.summary: A new type of neural network activation function based on recent physiological rate models for complex cells in visual area V1 is introduced, which results in orientation-selective features, similar to the receptive fields of complex cells.

core.title: Exploring Strategies for Training Deep Neural Networks
core.summary: These experiments confirm the hypothesis that the greedy layer-wise unsupervised training strategy helps the optimization by initializing weights in a region near a good local minimum, but also implicitly acts as a sort of regularization that brings better generalization and encourages internal distributed representations that are high-level abstractions of the input.

core.title: A hybrid Pareto model for asymmetric fat-tailed data: the univariate case
How do We Train Deep Architectures ?
core.summary: The motivations and principles regarding learning algorithms for deep architectures, in particular those exploiting as building blocks unsupervised learning of single-layer modelssuch as Restricted Boltzmann Machines, used to construct deeper models such as Deep Belief Networks are discussed.

core.title: Incorporating Functional Knowledge in Neural Networks
core.summary: A class of functions similar to multi-layer neural networks but that is a universal approximator of Lipschitz functions with these and other properties is proposed and applied to the task of modelling the price of call options.

core.title: Statistical Machine Learning Algorithms for Target Classification from Acoustic Signature
core.summary: This work compares two recently-introduced state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms, Support Vector Machines and Discriminative Restricted Boltzmann Machines, and develops how to use them to solve this difficult acoustic classification task, and obtains classification accuracy results that could make these techniques suitable for fielding on autonomous devices.

core.title: Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
Visualizing Higher-Layer Features of a Deep Network
core.summary: This paper contrast and compare several techniques applied on Stacked Denoising Autoencoders and Deep Belief Networks, trained on several vision datasets, and shows that good qualitative interpretations of high level features represented by such models are possible at the unit level.

core.title: A Hybrid Pareto Mixture for Conditional Asymmetric Fat-Tailed Distributions
Workshop summary: Workshop on learning feature hierarchies
Quadratic Features and Deep Architectures for Chunking
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Quadratic filters, a simplification of a theoretical model of V1 complex cells, reliably increase accuracy and logistic regression with quadratic filters outperforms a standard single hidden layer neural network.

core.title: Alternative time representation in dopamine models
core.summary: A general rate-based learning model based on long short-term memory networks that learns a time representation when needed that reproduces the known finding that trace conditioning is more difficult than delay conditioning and that the learned representation of the task can be highly dependent on the types of trials experienced during training.

core.title: Curriculum learning
core.summary: It is hypothesized that curriculum learning has both an effect on the speed of convergence of the training process to a minimum and on the quality of the local minima obtained: curriculum learning can be seen as a particular form of continuation method (a general strategy for global optimization of non-convex functions).

core.title: Justifying and Generalizing Contrastive Divergence
core.summary: An expansion of the log likelihood in undirected graphical models such as the restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM), where each term in the expansion is associated with a sample in a Gibbs chain alternating between two random variables, shows that its residual term converges to zero, justifying the use of a truncation of only a short Gibbs chain.

core.title: The Difficulty of Training Deep Architectures and the Effect of Unsupervised Pre-Training
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: The experiments confirm and clarify the advantage of unsupervised pre- training, and empirically show the influence of pre-training with respect to architecture depth, model capacity, and number of training examples.

core.title: An Infinite Factor Model Hierarchy Via a Noisy-Or Mechanism
core.summary: This work extends the latent factor model framework to two or more unbounded layers of latent factors so that each layer defines a conditional factorial prior distribution over the binary latent variables of the layer below via a noisy-or mechanism.

core.title: Non-parametric Regression between Riemannian Manifolds
MIREX TAGGING CONTEST : A DEEP NEURAL NET APPROACH ( DRAFT )
core.summary: The authors present one of their submission to MIREX 2008 audio tag classification contest, which uses a two hidden layers neural network.

core.title: Representational Power of Restricted Boltzmann Machines and Deep Belief Networks
core.summary: This work proves that adding hidden units yields strictly improved modeling power, while a second theorem shows that RBMs are universal approximators of discrete distributions and suggests a new and less greedy criterion for training RBMs within DBNs.

core.title: Adaptive Importance Sampling to Accelerate Training of a Neural Probabilistic Language Model
Extracting and composing robust features with denoising autoencoders
core.summary: This work introduces and motivate a new training principle for unsupervised learning of a representation based on the idea of making the learned representations robust to partial corruption of the input pattern.

core.title: Neural net language models
Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
Classification using discriminative restricted Boltzmann machines
core.summary: This paper presents an evaluation of different learning algorithms for RBMs which aim at introducing a discriminative component to RBM training and improve their performance as classifiers, and demonstrates how discriminating RBMs can also be successfully employed in a semi-supervised setting.

core.title: Zero-data Learning of New Tasks
core.summary: The main contributions of this work lie in the presentation of a general formalization of zero-data learning, in an experimental analysis of its properties and in empirical evidence showing that generalization is possible and significant in this context.

core.title: Augmented Functional Time Series Representation and Forecasting with Gaussian Processes
core.summary: A functional representation of time series is introduced which allows forecasts to be performed over an unspecified horizon with progressively-revealed information sets and a complete covariance matrix between forecasts at several time-steps is available.

core.title: Continuous Neural Networks
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: In the first approach proposed, a finite parametrization is possible, allowing gradient-based learning and a kernel machine can be made hyperparameter-free and still generalizes in spite of an absence of explicit regularization.

core.title: A Hybrid Pareto Model for Conditional Density Estimation of Asymmetric Fat-Tail Data
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: This work draws from Extreme Value Theory the tools to build a hybrid unimodal density having a parameter controlling the heaviness of the upper tail, a Gaussian whose upper tail has been replaced by a generalized Pareto tail.

core.title: On the challenge of learning complex functions.
core.summary: This chapter focuses on what is required for the learning of complex behaviors, in a mathematical sense, and brings forward two types of arguments which convey the message that many currently popular machine learning approaches to learning flexible functions have fundamental limitations that render them inappropriate for learning highly varying functions.

core.title: Learning the 2-D Topology of Images
core.summary: The surprising result presented here is that about as few as a thousand images are enough to approximately recover the relative locations of about a thousand pixels.

core.title: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 21, Proceedings of the Twenty-Second Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, December 8-11, 2008
Topmoumoute Online Natural Gradient Algorithm
core.summary: An efficient, general, online approximation to the natural gradient descent which is suited to large scale problems and much faster convergence in computation time and in number of iterations with TONGA than with stochastic gradient descent, even on very large datasets.

core.title: Scaling learning algorithms towards AI
core.summary: It is argued that deep architectures have the potential to generalize in non-local ways, i.e., beyond immediate neighbors, and that this is crucial in order to make progress on the kind of complex tasks required for artificial intelligence.

core.title: Forecasting and Trading Commodity Contract Spreads with Gaussian Processes
core.summary: A technique is introduced to exploit this joint autocovariance matrix of Gaussian Processes in order to profitably trade spreads, based on maximizing an information ratio criterion between candidate entry-exit points and constantly monitoring the position with revised forecasts as the spread realization unfolds.

core.title: On the Optimization of a Synaptic Learning Rule
core.summary: A new approach to neural modeling based on the idea of using an automated method to optimize the parameters of a synaptic learning rule and a theoretical analysis permitting to study the generalization property of such parametric learning rules is presented.

core.title: Deep Architectures for Baby AI
core.summary: Motivation: understanding intelligence, building AI, scaling to large scale learning of complex functions, and measuring the impact of artificial intelligence on the real world.

core.title: Noisy K Best-Paths for Approximate Dynamic Programming with Application to Portfolio Optimization
core.summary: It is shown that using a non-additive criterion (incremental Sharpe Ratio) yields a noisy K-best-paths extraction problem, that can give substantially improved performance.

core.title: An empirical evaluation of deep architectures on problems with many factors of variation
core.summary: A series of experiments indicate that these models with deep architectures show promise in solving harder learning problems that exhibit many factors of variation.

core.title: Learning Deep Architectures for AI
core.summary: The motivations and principles regarding learning algorithms for deep architectures, in particular those exploiting as building blocks unsupervised learning of single-layer modelssuch as Restricted Boltzmann Machines, used to construct deeper models such as Deep Belief Networks are discussed.

core.title: Proposed Algorithm : Algorithm
core.summary: This work proposes a compression algorithm that uses space proportional to the number of frequency classes, which is, quite interestingly, always smaller or equal to the size of the alphabet.

core.title: TRAINING A NEURAL NETWORK WITH A FINANCIAL CRITERION RATHER THAN A PREDICTION CRITERION
Greedy Layer-Wise Training of Deep Networks
core.summary: These experiments confirm the hypothesis that the greedy layer-wise unsupervised training strategy mostly helps the optimization, by initializing weights in a region near a good local minimum, giving rise to internal distributed representations that are high-level abstractions of the input, bringing better generalization.

core.title: Large-Scale Algorithms
Entropy Regularization
Distributed Representation Prediction for Generalization to New Words
core.summary: This work considers the distributed representations of symbols of words as predictions from low-level or domain-knowledge features of words, which demonstrates the success of this approach in learning meaningful representations and in providing improved accuracy, especially for new words.

core.title: Neural Probabilistic Language Models
core.summary: This work proposes to fight the curse of dimensionality by learning a distributed representation for words which allows each training sentence to inform the model about an exponential number of semantically neighboring sentences, and incorporates this new language model into a state-of-the-art speech recognizer of conversational speech.

core.title: Collaborative Filtering on a Family of Biological Targets
core.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
core.summary: This work shows an example of a multi-target neural network that can use family information to produce a predictive model of an undersampled target, and evaluates JRank, a kernel-based method designed for collaborative filtering.

core.title: Nonlocal Estimation of Manifold Structure
core.summary: It is claimed and presented that a large class of manifold learning algorithms that are essentially local and can be framed as kernel learning algorithms will suffer from the curse of dimensionality, at the dimension of the true underlying manifold.

core.title: Label Propagation and Quadratic Criterion
PROC OF THE IEEE NOVEMBER Gradient Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
core.summary: Convolutional Neural Networks that are specif ically designed to deal with the variability of D shapes are shown to outperform all other techniques and demonstrate the advantage of global training and the exibility of Graph Transformer Networks.

core.title: A Hybrid Pareto Model for Asymmetric Fat-Tail Data
The K Best-Paths Approach to Approximate Dynamic Programming with Application to Portfolio Optimization
core.summary: A general method to transform a non-markovian sequential decision problem into a supervised learning problem using a K-best-paths algorithm is described and an application in financial portfolio management where a controller can train a controller to directly optimize a Sharpe Ratio utility function is considered.

core.title: Generalizing to a zero-data task : a computational chemistry case study
core.summary: It is shown that it is indeed possible to learn a shared representation of the tasks that allows to generalize to a new task for which no training data are available, and this algorithm can be readily used by pharmaceutical companies for virtual screening campaigns.

core.title: Reassuring and Troubling Views on Graph-Based Semi-Supervised Learning
Learning Influence among Interacting Markov Chains
core.summary: A model that learns the influence of interacting Markov chains within a team using a dynamic Bayesian network with a two-level structure: individual-level and group-level.

core.title: Bias in Estimating the Variance of K-Fold Cross-Validation
core.summary: The main theorem shows that there exists no universal (valid under all distributions) unbiased estimator of the variance of K-fold cross-validation, based on a single computation of the K- fold cross- validation estimator.

core.title: Convex Neural Networks
core.summary: Training multi-layer neural networks in which the number of hidden units is learned can be viewed as a convex optimization problem, which involves an infinite number of variables but can be solved by incrementally inserting a hidden unit at a time.

core.title: Greedy Spectral Embedding
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: A greedy selection procedure for this subset of m examples, based on the featurespace distance between a candidate example and the span of the previously chosen ones, to estimate the embedding function based on all the data.

core.title: Non-Local Manifold Parzen Windows
core.summary: This work presents a non-local non-parametric density estimator that builds upon previously proposed Gaussian mixture models with regularized covariance matrices to take into account the local shape of the manifold.

core.title: The Curse of Dimensionality for Local Kernel Machines
core.summary: A series of theoretical arguments support the claim that a large class of modern learning algorithms based on local kernels are sensitive to the curse of dimensionality, including local manifold learning algorithms such as Isomap and LLE, support vector classifiers with Gaussian or other local kernels, and graph-based semisupervised learning algorithms using a local similarity function.

core.title: The Curse of Highly Variable Functions for Local Kernel Machines
core.summary: A series of theoretical arguments are presented supporting the claim that a large class of modern learning algorithms that rely solely on the smoothness prior - with similarity between examples expressed with a local kernel - are sensitive to the curse of dimensionality, or more precisely to the variability of the target.

core.title: Hierarchical Probabilistic Neural Network Language Model
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: A hierarchical decomposition of the conditional probabilities that yields a speed-up of about 200 both during training and recognition, constrained by the prior knowledge extracted from the WordNet semantic hierarchy is introduced.

core.title: Selective small molecule peptidomimetic ligands of TrkC and TrkA receptors afford discrete or complete neurotrophic activities.
core.summary: The high rate of hits identified suggests that focused minilibraries may be desirable for developing bioactive ligands of cell surface receptors, and small, selective, proteolytically stable ligands with defined biological activity may have therapeutic potential.

core.title: Unsupervised Sense Disambiguation Using Bilingual Probabilistic Models
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Two probabilistic models for unsupervised word-sense disambiguation using parallel corpora are described, one of which is a hierarchical model that uses a concept latent variable to relate different language specific sense labels.

core.title: Locally Weighted Full Covariance Gaussian Density Estimation
Markovian Models for Sequential
core.summary: The basics ofHMMs are summarized and several recent related learning algorithms and extensions of HMMs including in particular hybrids of HM Ms with arti cial neural networks are reviewed.

core.title: Discovering Shared Structure in Manifold Learning
core.summary: This analysis suggests non-local manifold learning algorithms which attempt to discover shared structure in the tangent planes at different positions, which has parameters that are shared across space rather than estimated based on the local neighborhood, as in current non-parametric manifolds learning algorithms.

core.title: Semi-supervised Learning by Entropy Minimization
core.summary: This framework, which motivates minimum entropy regularization, enables to incorporate unlabeled data in the standard supervised learning, and includes other approaches to the semi-supervised problem as particular or limiting cases.

core.title: Approche statistique pour le repérage de mots informatifs dans les textes oraux
core.summary: L’évaluation est effectuée en comparant la sortie du système avec les réponses de formulaires d’extraction d”information prédéfinis.

core.title: Repérage de mots informatifs dans les textes conversationnels
Learning Eigenfunctions Links Spectral Embedding and Kernel PCA
core.summary: A direct relation is shown between spectral embedding methods and kernel principal components analysis and how both are special cases of a more general learning problem: learning the principal eigenfunctions of an operator defined from a kernel and the unknown data-generating density.

core.title: Non-Local Manifold Tangent Learning
core.summary: It is claimed and presented arguments that a large class of manifold learning algorithms that are essentially local and can be framed as kernel learning algorithms will suffer from the curse of dimensionality, at the dimension of the true underlying manifold.

core.title: Efficient Non-Parametric Function Induction in Semi-Supervised Learning
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: Experiments show that the proposed non-parametric algorithms which provide an estimated continuous label for the given unlabeled examples are extended to function induction algorithms that correspond to the minimization of a regularization criterion applied to an out-of-sample example, and happens to have the form of a Parzen windows regressor.

core.title: Locally Linear Embedding for dimensionality reduction in QSAR
core.summary: Locally Linear Embedding (LLE), a local non-linear dimensionality reduction technique, that can statistically discover a low-dimensional representation of the chemical data, is introduced.

core.title: Markovian Models for Sequential Data
core.summary: The basics ofHMMs are summarized and several recent related learning algorithms and extensions of HMMs including in particular hybrids of HM Ms with arti cial neural networks are reviewed.

core.title: Brain Inspired Reinforcement Learning
core.summary: New reinforcement learning algorithms inspired by neurological evidence that provides potential new approaches to the feature construction problem are developed and evaluated.

core.title: Estimation de densité conditionnelle lorsque l'hypothèse de normalité est insatisfaisante
Learning Eigenfunctions of Similarity: Linking Spectral Clustering and Kernel PCA
core.summary: A direct equivalence is shown between spectral clustering and kernel PCA, and how both are special cases of a more general learning problem, that of learning the principal eigenfunctions of a kernel, when the functions are from a Hilbert space whose inner product is dened with respect to a density model.

core.title: Quick Training of Probabilistic Neural Nets by Importance Sampling
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: Inspired by the contrastive divergence model, sampling-based methods which require network passes only for the observed “positive example” and a few sampled negative example words are proposed and evaluated.

core.title: Out-of-Sample Extensions for LLE, Isomap, MDS, Eigenmaps, and Spectral Clustering
core.summary: A unified framework for extending Local Linear Embedding, Isomap, Laplacian Eigenmaps, Multi-Dimensional Scaling as well as for Spectral Clustering is provided.

core.title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model
core.summary: This work reports on experiments using neural networks for the probability function, showing on two text corpora that the proposed approach very significantly improves on a state-of-the-art trigram model.

core.title: Comment améliorer la capacité de généralisation des algorithmes d'apprentissage pour la prise de décisions financières
Statistical Learning Algorithms Applied to Automobile Insurance Ratemaking
core.summary: This paper presents a meta-analyses of six models used for Bayesian inference of Neural Networks’ Representation of Nonlinear Interactions and concludes that three of them, the Constant Model and the Linear Model, are good candidates forBayesian inference.

core.title: Estimators of Variance for K-Fold Cross-Validation
core.summary: Estimating the variance of EPE, the estimate provided by K-fold cross-validation, is focused on, which should provide means to build confidence intervals on EPE and to derive statistics to test the significance of observed differences between algorithms.

core.title: Bias learning, knowledge sharing
core.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE-INNS-ENNS International Joint Conference on Neural Networks. IJCNN 2000. Neural Computing: New Challenges and Perspectives for the New Millennium

core.title: Extracting Hidden Sense Probabilities from Bitexts
core.summary: A probabilistic model that is inspired by Diab & Resnik’s algorithm to extract disambiguation information from aligned bilingual texts using WordNet and the fact that word ambiguities are not always the same in the two languages.

core.title: On Out-of-Sample Statistics for Financial Time-Series
Input Decay : Simple and Effective Soft Variable Selection
Model Selection for Small Sample Regression
